For instance, ≤ (less than or equal to) is a total order on integers, that is, for any two integers, one of them is less than or equal to the other. Formal Definition: A total order is a relation that is reflexive , transitive , antisymmetric , and total. Also known as linear order.

nodes.label: tournament

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: tournament

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines tournament as: Find the maximum of a set of n elements in ⌈log n⌉ "rounds" (passes) by "playing" (comparing) pairs of elements and advancing the winner (greater) of each pair to the next round. It takes n-1 comparisons, like linear search , but may be parallelized, extended to also find the second greatest element, etc.

nodes.label: tractable

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: tractable

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines tractable as: A problem which has an algorithm which computes all instances of it in polynomial time .

nodes.label: transition

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: transition

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines transition as: The change from one state to another in a finite state machine . Analogously, an edge in a directed graph . Also known as state transition, move.

nodes.label: transition function

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: transitionfn

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines transition function as: A function of the current state and input giving the next state of a finite state machine or Turing machine .

nodes.label: transitive

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: transitive

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines transitive as: A binary relation R for which a R b and b R c implies a R c.

nodes.label: transitive reduction

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: transitiveReduction

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines transitive reduction as: The transitive reduction of a directed graph G is the directed graph G' with the smallest number of edges such that for every path between vertices in G, G' has a path between those vertices.

nodes.label: transpose sequential search

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: transposeSeqSearch

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines transpose sequential search as: Search an array or list by checking items one at a time. If the value is found, swap it with its predecessor so it is found faster next time. Also known as self-organizing sequential search.

nodes.label: traveling salesman

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: travelingSalesman

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines traveling salesman as: Find a path through a weighted graph that starts and ends at the same vertex , includes every other vertex exactly once, and minimizes the total cost of edges . Also known as TSP.

nodes.label: treap

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: treap

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines treap as: A binary search tree in which nodes have another key , called the priority. Operations also keep the nodes heap ordered with regard to the priority.

nodes.label: tree automaton

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: treeAutomaton

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines tree automaton as: An extension of a finite state machine that operates on n-ary constructors. Where a finite state automaton reaches a new state with a single state and character, a tree automaton takes n states and constructors. Tree automata may be top-down (starting from the root ) or bottom-up (starting from the leaves ), and deterministic or nondeterministic .

nodes.label: tree traversal

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: treeTraversal

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines tree traversal as: A technique for processing the nodes of a tree in some order.

nodes.label: tree contraction

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: treecontrctn

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines tree contraction as: Contracting a tree by removing some of the nodes.

nodes.label: tree editing problem

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: treeedit

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines tree editing problem as: The problem of finding an edit script of minimum cost which transforms a given tree into another given tree.

nodes.label: treesort (1)

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: treesort1

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines treesort (1) as: A sort algorithm that first builds a binary search tree of the keys , then accesses the keys with an in-order traversal .

nodes.label: treesort (2)

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: treesort2

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines treesort (2) as: Variants of heapsort .

nodes.label: triangle inequality

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: trianglnqlty

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines triangle inequality as: The property that a complete weighted graph satisfies weight(u,v) ≤ weight(u,w) + weight(w,v) for all vertices u, v, w. Informally, the graph has no short cuts.

nodes.label: triconnected graph

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: triconnectedGraph

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines triconnected graph as: A connected graph such that deleting any two vertices (and incident edges ) results in a graph that is still connected.

nodes.label: trinary function

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: trinaryfunc

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines trinary function as: A function with three arguments.

nodes.label: tripartition

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: tripartition

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines tripartition as: To partition array elements into three groups.

nodes.label: Turing reduction

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: turingredctn

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines Turing reduction as: A reduction computable by an oracle Turing machine that halts for all inputs.

nodes.label: twin grid file

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: twingridfl

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines twin grid file as: A point access method which is two simultaneous grid files . Points are shuffled between the primary and secondary file to minimize the total size.

nodes.label: 2-3-4 tree

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: two34tree

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines 2-3-4 tree as: A B-tree of order 4, that is, internal nodes have two, three, or four children .

nodes.label: Two Way algorithm

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: twoWay

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines Two Way algorithm as: Partition ("factor") the pattern , x, into left, x l , and right, x r , parts in such a way to optimize searching. Compare x r left to right then, if it matches, compare x l right to left.

nodes.label: two-dimensional

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: twodimensnal

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines two-dimensional as: Dealing with or restricted to a plane. An organization where location can be completely described with exactly two orthogonal axes.

nodes.label: two-level grid file

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: twolevgrid

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines two-level grid file as: A point access method which is two levels of grid files . The first level addresses second level grid files.

nodes.label: two-way merge sort

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: twowaymrgsrt

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines two-way merge sort as: A k-way merge sort that sorts a data stream using repeated merges. It distributes the input into two streams by repeatedly reading a block of input that fits in memory, a run , sorting it, then writing it to the next stream. It merges runs from the two streams into an output stream. It then repeatedly distributes the runs in the output stream to the two streams and merges them until there is a single sorted output.

nodes.label: UB-tree

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: ubtree

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines UB-tree as: Refers to either universal B-tree or unlimited branching tree .

nodes.label: unary function

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: unaryfunc

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines unary function as: A function which takes one argument.

nodes.label: unbiased coin flipping algorithm

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: unbiasedCoinFlipAlgo

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines unbiased coin flipping algorithm as: To get unbiased random bits, flip a coin twice. If it comes up heads then tails, the result bit is 1. It it comes up tails then heads, the result is 0. Repeat the double flips until one of these occurs.

nodes.label: uncomputable function

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: uncomputableFunction

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines uncomputable function as: A function that cannot be computed by any algorithm --- equivalently, not by any Turing machine .

nodes.label: undecidable language

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: undecidableLanguage

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines undecidable language as: A language for which the membership cannot be decided by an algorithm --- equivalently, cannot be recognized by a Turing machine that halts for all inputs.

nodes.label: undecidable problem

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: undecidableProblem

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines undecidable problem as: A problem that cannot be solved for all cases by any algorithm whatsoever---equivalently, whose associated language cannot be recognized by a Turing machine that halts for all inputs.

nodes.label: undirected graph

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: undirectedGraph

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines undirected graph as: A graph whose edges are unordered pairs of vertices . That is, each edge connects two vertices. Formal Definition: A graph G is a pair (V,E), where V is a set of vertices, and E is a set of edges between the vertices E ⊆ {{u,v} | u, v ∈ V}. If the graph does not allow self-loops , adjacency is irreflexive , that is E ⊆ {{u,v} | u, v ∈ V ∧ u ≠ v}.

nodes.label: uniform circuit complexity

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: uniformCircuitComplexity

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines uniform circuit complexity as: The study of complexity classes defined by uniform circuit families .

nodes.label: uniform circuit family

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: uniformCircuitFamily

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines uniform circuit family as: A sequence of circuits , one for each input length n, that can be efficiently generated by a Turing machine .

nodes.label: uniform hashing

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: uniformhashn

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines uniform hashing as: A conceptual method of open addressing for a hash table . A collision is resolved by putting the item in the next empty place given by a probe sequence which is independent of sequences for all other key .

nodes.label: uniform matrix

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: uniformmatrx

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines uniform matrix as: A matrix having the same number of items in each row.

nodes.label: union

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: union

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines union as: The union of two sets is a set having all members in either set.

nodes.label: union of automata

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: unionautoma

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines union of automata as: Find an automaton that accepts everything which the automata accept individually.

nodes.label: universal Turing machine

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: universalTur

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines universal Turing machine as: A Turing machine that is capable of simulating any other Turing machine by encoding the latter.

nodes.label: universal hashing

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: universalhsh

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines universal hashing as: A scheme that chooses randomly from a set of hash functions .

nodes.label: universal state

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: universalstt

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines universal state as: A state in an alternating Turing machine from which the machine accepts only if all possible moves lead to acceptance.

nodes.label: universe

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: universe

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines universe as: All potential elements of a set .

nodes.label: unlimited branching tree

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: unlimitedBranchingTree

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines unlimited branching tree as: A forest of ordered trees used to contain ordered lists . The root of each tree is unique. An ordered list is represented by a traversal from the root (first element of the list) to a leaf (last list element). Lists with common prefixes share nodes. The last node in common has one child for each list. This allows rapid searches for subset inclusion of sequences.

nodes.label: unranking

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: unrank

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines unranking as: Given a ranking, r, generate the r th permutation of n elements.

nodes.label: UnShuffle sort

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: unshufflsort

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines UnShuffle sort as: A distribution sort with two phases. In the first phase, the inputs are distributed among doubly-ended queues keeping the items in each queue ordered and creating a new queue when there is no place on an existing queue. The second phase is an ideal merge in which the item to be removed is determined by keeping the queues in a priority queue .

nodes.label: unsolvable problem

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: unsolvableProblem

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines unsolvable problem as: A computational problem that cannot be solved by a Turing machine . The associated function is called an uncomputable function .

nodes.label: unsorted list

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: unsortedList

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines unsorted list as: A list whose order of items, if any, is not known.

nodes.label: upper triangular matrix

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: upperTriangularMatrix

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines upper triangular matrix as: A matrix that is only defined at (i,j) when i ≤ j.

nodes.label: van Emde-Boas priority queue

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: vanemdeboas

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines van Emde-Boas priority queue as: An efficient implementation of priority queues where insert, delete, get minimum, get maximum, etc. take O(log log N) time, where N is the total possible number of keys . Depending on the circumstance, the implementation is null (if the queue is empty), an integer (if the queue has one integer), a bit vector of size N (if N is small), or a special data structure : an array of priority queues, called the bottom queues, and one more priority queue of array indexes of the bottom queues.

nodes.label: vehicle routing problem

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: vehicleRouting

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines vehicle routing problem as: Find an optimal route of one or more vehicles through a graph . Also known as VRP.

nodes.label: Venn diagram

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: venndiagram

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines Venn diagram as: A visual depiction of membership in sets according to binary properties, using overlapping ovals to divide the plane into regions. Regions inside an oval have the property the oval represents, while regions outside it do not have the property. Regions are shaded to show combinations of properties (or sets) of interest, or elements are placed in regions corresponding to their properties (or membership).

nodes.label: vertex connectivity

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: vertexConnectivity

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines vertex connectivity as: (1) The smallest number of vertices whose deletion causes a connected graph to not be connected. (2) For a pair of vertices s and t in a graph, the smallest number of vertices whose deletion will separate s from t.

nodes.label: vertex coloring

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: vertexcolor

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines vertex coloring as: An assignment of colors (or any distinct marks) to the vertices of a graph . Strictly speaking, a coloring is proper if no two adjacent vertices have the same color.

nodes.label: vertex cover

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: vertexcover

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines vertex cover as: A set of vertices in an undirected graph where every edge connects at least one vertex. The vertex cover problem is to find a minimum size set and is NP-complete .

nodes.label: vertical visibility map

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: vertical

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines vertical visibility map as: A partition of the plane into regions by drawing a vertical straight line through each vertex p of a planar straight-line graph until it intersects an edge e of the graph or extends to infinity. The edge e is said to be vertically visible from p.

nodes.label: visibility map

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: visibilityMap

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines visibility map as: A planar subdivision that encodes the visibility information, that is, which points are mutually visible .

nodes.label: visible

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: visible

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines visible as: Two points p and q are visible if the straight line segment between them does not intersect any other object, edge, etc.

nodes.label: Viterbi algorithm

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: viterbiAlgorithm

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines Viterbi algorithm as: An algorithm to compute the optimal (most likely) state sequence in a hidden Markov model given a sequence of observed outputs.

nodes.label: Vitter's algorithm

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: vittersAlgorithm

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines Vitter's algorithm as: An adaptive Huffman coding scheme. Typically this produces codings the same length as or shorter than static Huffman coding . In the worst case , this uses one more bit per codeword .

nodes.label: walk

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: walk

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines walk as: A path in which edges may be repeated.

nodes.label: weak-heap

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: weakheap

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines weak-heap as: A relaxed heap satisfying the following three conditions: (1) every key in the right subtree of a node is greater than the key stored in the node itself, (2) the root has no left child , and (3) leaves are only found on the last two levels of the tree.

nodes.label: weak-heap sort

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: weakheapsort

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines weak-heap sort as: A sort algorithm that builds a weak-heap , then repeatedly extracts the maximum item. In the worst case , the run time is O(n log n + 0.1 n) .

nodes.label: weighted, directed graph

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: weightedDigraph

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines weighted, directed graph as: A directed graph that has a weight, or numeric value, associated with each edge .

nodes.label: window

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: window

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines window as: substring of the text that is aligned with the pattern .

nodes.label: witness

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: witness

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines witness as: (1) a structure providing an easily verified bound on the optimal value of an optimization problem . Typically used in the analysis of an approximation algorithm to prove the performance guarantee . (2) a mismatch of two symbols of string y at a distance of d is a "witness" to the fact that in no subject y could occur twice at a distance of exactly d positions (equivalently, that d cannot be a period of y).

nodes.label: work

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: work

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines work as: The total number of operations taken by a computation.

nodes.label: work-depth model

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: workdepthmdl

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines work-depth model as: A model of parallel computation in which one keeps track of the total work and depth of a computation without worrying about how it maps onto a machine.

nodes.label: work-efficient

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: workefficint

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines work-efficient as: A parallel algorithm which asymptotically requires at most a constant factor more work than the best known sequential algorithm or the optimal work.

nodes.label: work-preserving

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: workpreserv

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines work-preserving as: A translation of an algorithm from one model of computation to another in which the work is the same in both models, to within a constant factor.

nodes.label: worst-case execution time

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: worstCaseExecutionTime

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines worst-case execution time as: The execution time of an algorithm in the worst case . Also known as WCET.

nodes.label: worst-case minimum access

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: worstCaseMinimumAccess

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines worst-case minimum access as: A figure of merit for a family of searches, the "best" is the search that takes the minimum accesses in the worst case .

nodes.label: worst case

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: worstcase

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines worst case as: (1) The situation or input that forces an algorithm or data structure to take the most time or resources. (2) Having to do with this situation or input.

nodes.label: worst-case cost

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: worstcaseCost

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines worst-case cost as: The highest possible use of resources of an algorithm , which occurs for the most pessimistic, or worst possible, input.

nodes.label: xor

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: xor

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines xor as: "Exclusive OR" or "not equal to" function: 0 XOR 0 = 0, 0 XOR 1 = 1, 1 XOR 0 = 1, 1 XOR 1 = 0. Also known as exclusive or.

nodes.label: Zeller's congruence

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: zellersCongruence

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines Zeller's congruence as: An algorithm to find the day of the week for any date.

nodes.label: 0-based indexing

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: zeroBasedIndexing

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines 0-based indexing as: Indexing (an array ) beginning with 0.

nodes.label: 0-ary function

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: zeroaryfunc

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines 0-ary function as: A function that takes no arguments. Also known as nullary function.

nodes.label: Zhu-Takaoka

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: zhuTakaoka

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines Zhu-Takaoka as: A string matching algorithm that is a variant of the Boyer-Moore algorithm. It uses two consecutive text characters to compute the bad character shift. It is faster when the alphabet or pattern is small, but the skip table grows quickly, slowing the pre-processing phase.

nodes.label: Zipfian distribution

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: zipfian

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines Zipfian distribution as: A distribution of probabilities of occurrence that follows Zipf's law . Also known as Yule distribution.

nodes.label: zipper

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: zipper

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines zipper as: A data structure equivalent to a binary tree that is "opened" so that some node is accessible. It consists of a pair: the current node, along with information to reconstruct the tree. Reconstruction information is called the path or context. A move-to-left-child operation returns the left subtree, along with a new path, which has (i) a Left value, (ii) the current node, (iii) the right subtree, and (iv) any previous path. A similar operation moves to the right child. A move-up operation returns a tree rebuilt from the path information and the current node, along with the previous path.

nodes.label: ZPP

sources.title: NIST Dictionary of Algorithms and Data Structures: zpp

nodes.summary: NIST DADS defines ZPP as: The class of languages for which a membership computation by a probabilistic Turing machine halts in polynomial time with no false acceptances or rejections, but randomly some "I don't know" answers. "ZPP" means " Z ero error P robability in P olynomial" time. Formal Definition: For a language, S, there exists a probabilistic Turing machine , M, that halts in polynomial time . M (correctly) accepts or rejects the string or, randomly, halts in an "I don't know" state.

nodes.label: Bionics

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D001701

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Bionics as: The study of systems, particularly electronic systems, which function after the manner of, in a manner characteristic of, or resembling living systems. Also, the science of applying biological techniques and principles to the design of electronic systems.

nodes.label: Biotechnology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D001709

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Biotechnology as: Body of knowledge related to the use of organisms, cells or cell-derived constituents for the purpose of developing products which are technically, scientifically and clinically useful. Alteration of biologic function at the molecular level (i.e., GENETIC ENGINEERING ) is a central focus; laboratory methods used include TRANSFECTION and CLONING technologies, sequence and structure analysis algorithms, computer databases, and gene and protein structure function analysis and prediction.

nodes.label: Nanotechnology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D036103

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Nanotechnology as: The development and use of techniques to study physical phenomena and construct structures in the nanoscale size range or smaller.

nodes.label: Andrology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D033441

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Andrology as: A scientific or medical discipline concerning the study of male reproductive biology, diseases of the male genital organs, and male infertility. Major areas of interest include ENDOCRINOLOGY ; SPERMATOGENESIS ; SEMEN ANALYSIS ; FERTILIZATION ; CONTRACEPTION ; and CRYOPRESERVATION .

nodes.label: Audiology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D001298

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Audiology as: Allied medical specialty that studies hearing and hearing impairment.

nodes.label: Cardiology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D002309

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Cardiology as: The study of the heart, its physiology, and its functions.

nodes.label: Dermatology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D003880

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Dermatology as: A medical specialty concerned with the skin, its structure, functions, diseases, and treatment.

nodes.label: Gastroenterology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D005762

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Gastroenterology as: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of the physiology and diseases of the digestive system and related structures (esophagus, liver, gallbladder, and pancreas).

nodes.label: Gynecology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D006176

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Gynecology as: A medical-surgical specialty concerned with the physiology and disorders primarily of the female genital tract, as well as female endocrinology and reproductive physiology.

nodes.label: Hematology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D006405

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Hematology as: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with morphology, physiology, and pathology of the blood and blood-forming tissues.

nodes.label: Neonatology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D009359

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Neonatology as: A subspecialty of Pediatrics concerned with the newborn infant.

nodes.label: Nephrology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D009398

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Nephrology as: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the anatomy, physiology, and pathology of the kidney.

nodes.label: Neurology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D009462

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Neurology as: A medical specialty concerned with the study of the structures, functions, and diseases of the nervous system.

nodes.label: Neuropathology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D000069338

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Neuropathology as: The branch of medicine and biomedical science concerned with diseases of the nervous system.

nodes.label: Ophthalmology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D009885

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Ophthalmology as: A surgical specialty concerned with the structure and function of the eye and the medical and surgical treatment of its defects and diseases.

nodes.label: Pharmacology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D010600

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Pharmacology as: The study of the origin, nature, properties, and actions of drugs and their effects on living organisms.

nodes.label: Psychopharmacology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D011600

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Psychopharmacology as: The study of the effects of drugs on mental and behavioral activity.

nodes.label: Radiology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D011871

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Radiology as: A specialty concerned with the use of x-ray and other forms of radiant energy in the diagnosis and treatment of disease.

nodes.label: Rheumatology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D012219

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Rheumatology as: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of inflammatory or degenerative processes and metabolic derangement of connective tissue structures which pertain to a variety of musculoskeletal disorders, such as arthritis.

nodes.label: Serology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D012699

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Serology as: The study of serum, especially of antigen-antibody reactions in vitro.

nodes.label: Thanatology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D013795

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Thanatology as: The study of the theory, philosophy, and doctrine of death.

nodes.label: Toxicology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D014116

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Toxicology as: The science concerned with the detection, chemical composition, and biological action of toxic substances or poisons and the treatment and prevention of toxic manifestations.

nodes.label: Traumatology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D014194

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Traumatology as: The medical specialty which deals with WOUNDS and INJURIES as well as resulting disability and disorders from physical traumas.

nodes.label: Urology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D014572

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Urology as: A surgical specialty concerned with the study, diagnosis, and treatment of diseases of the urinary tract in both sexes, and the genital tract in the male. Common urological problems include urinary obstruction, URINARY INCONTINENCE , infections, and UROGENITAL NEOPLASMS .

nodes.label: Paleography

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D010162

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Paleography as: The study of ancient inscriptions and modes of writing. It includes the deciphering of manuscripts and other forms to determine their date, provenance, etc. (Webster's 1st ed)

nodes.label: Philology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D010680

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Philology as: The study of literature in its widest sense, including grammar, etymology, criticism, literary history, language history, linguistic history, systems of writing, and anything else that is relevant to literature or language viewed as literature. Philology as a discipline has both philosophical and scientific overtones.

nodes.label: Theology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D028725

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Theology as: The study of religion and religious belief, or a particular system or school of religious beliefs and teachings (from online Cambridge Dictionary of American English, 2000 and WordNet: An Electronic Lexical Database, 1997)

nodes.label: Cognitive psychology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D000090182
NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D019336

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Cognitive psychology as: Branch of psychology that explores the operation of mental processes related to perceiving, attending, thinking, language, and memory, mainly through inferences from behavior. (APA Dictionary of Psychology. https://dictionary.apa.org/cognitive-psychology, accessed 3/22/2021).

nodes.label: Computational biology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D019295

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Computational biology as: A field of biology concerned with the development of techniques for the collection and manipulation of biological data, and the use of such data to make biological discoveries or predictions. This field encompasses all computational methods and theories for solving biological problems including manipulation of models and datasets.

nodes.label: Psycholinguistics

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D011578

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Psycholinguistics as: A discipline concerned with relations between messages and the characteristics of individuals who select and interpret them; it deals directly with the processes of encoding (phonetics) and decoding (psychoacoustics) as they relate states of messages to states of communicators.

nodes.label: Cryobiology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D000073920

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Cryobiology as: The study of biological materials or systems subjected to temperatures below their normal range.

nodes.label: Cytology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D000093222

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Cytology as: The study of single cell as a unit of living organisms. Cytopathology, a branch of this discipline, studies structural changes of cells in diseases and is used in diagnosing diseases.

nodes.label: Embryology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D004626

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Embryology as: The study of the development of an organism during the embryonic and fetal stages of life.

nodes.label: Genomics

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D023281

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Genomics as: The systematic study of the complete DNA sequences ( GENOME ) of organisms. Included is construction of complete genetic, physical, and transcript maps, and the analysis of this structural genomic information on a global scale such as in GENOME WIDE ASSOCIATION STUDIES .

nodes.label: Glycobiology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D000099126

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Glycobiology as: The study of the structure, function, and biology of carbohydrates (sugars) and carbohydrate-containing molecules, known as glycans, in biological systems.

nodes.label: Neurobiology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D009446

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Neurobiology as: The study of the structure, growth, activities, and functions of NEURONS and the NERVOUS SYSTEM .

nodes.label: Pharmacognosy

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D010598

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Pharmacognosy as: The science of drugs prepared from natural-sources including preparations from PLANTS , animals, and other organisms as well as MINERALS and other substances included in MATERIA MEDICA . The therapeutic usage of plants is PHYTOTHERAPY .

nodes.label: Physiology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D010827

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Physiology as: The biological science concerned with the life-supporting properties, functions, and processes of living organisms or their parts.

nodes.label: Proteomics

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D040901

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Proteomics as: The systematic study of the complete complement of proteins ( PROTEOME ) of organisms.

nodes.label: Sociobiology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D035503

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Sociobiology as: The comparative study of social organization in animals including humans, especially with regard to its genetic basis and evolutionary history. (Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed)

nodes.label: Teratology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D018600

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Teratology as: A branch of embryology for the study of congenital malformations and developmental abnormalities.

nodes.label: Photobiology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D018462

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Photobiology as: The branch of biology dealing with the effect of light on organisms.

nodes.label: Radiobiology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D011853

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Radiobiology as: Study of the scientific principles, mechanisms, and effects of the interaction of ionizing radiation with living matter. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

nodes.label: Rheology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D012212

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Rheology as: The study of the deformation and flow of matter, usually liquids or fluids, and of the plastic flow of solids. The concept covers consistency, dilatancy, liquefaction, resistance to flow, shearing, thixotrophy, and VISCOSITY .

nodes.label: Criminology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D003418

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Criminology as: The study of crime and criminals with special reference to the personality factors and social conditions leading toward, or away from crime.

nodes.label: Demography

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D003710

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Demography as: Statistical interpretation and description of a population with reference to distribution, composition, or structure.

nodes.label: Ethnology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D005007

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethnology as: The comparative and theoretical study of culture, often synonymous with cultural anthropology.

nodes.label: Neuropsychology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D009484

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Neuropsychology as: A branch of psychology which investigates the correlation between experience or behavior and the basic neurophysiological processes. The term neuropsychology stresses the dominant role of the nervous system. It is a more narrowly defined field than physiological psychology or psychophysiology.

nodes.label: Psychopathology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D011599

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Psychopathology as: The study of significant causes and processes in the development of mental illness.

nodes.label: Sexology

sources.title: NLM MeSH descriptor or exact lookup: https://meshb.nlm.nih.gov/record/ui?ui=D044347

nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Sexology as: This discipline concerns the study of SEXUALITY , and the application of sexual knowledge such as sexual attitudes, psychology, and SEXUAL BEHAVIOR . Scope of application generally includes educational ( SEX EDUCATION ), clinical ( SEX COUNSELING ), and other settings.

nodes.label: Fermi-LAT GRB 090510 photon observations

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.3463

nodes.summary: Source-attributed description: The photon observations of GRB090510 collected by Fermi-LAT are analyzed in the cited work to constrain energy-dependent vacuum dispersion, under its stated source and propagation assumptions.

nodes.label: LZ WIMP-search data from 280 live days

sources.title: Retained source for unfinished atlas records: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17036

nodes.summary: Source-attributed description: The cited LZ WIMP-search analysis uses detector data corresponding to 4.2 ± 0.1 tonne-years of total exposure over 280 live days. It reports no excess over expected backgrounds.

nodes.label: Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Medicine as: The art and science of studying, performing research on, preventing, diagnosing, and treating disease, as well as the maintenance of health.

nodes.label: Addiction Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Addiction Medicine as: A medical specialty focused on the diagnosis and treatment of ADDICTIVE BEHAVIOR disorders, including SUBSTANCE-RELATED DISORDERS and IMPULSE CONTROL DISORDERS ; and the management of co-occurring medical and psychiatric conditions

nodes.label: Adolescent Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Adolescent Medicine as: A branch of medicine pertaining to the diagnosis and treatment of diseases occurring during the period of ADOLESCENCE .

nodes.label: Aerospace Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Aerospace Medicine as: That branch of medicine dealing with the studies and effects of flight through the atmosphere or in space upon the human body and with the prevention or cure of physiological or psychological malfunctions arising from these effects. (from NASA Thesaurus)

nodes.label: Allergy and Immunology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Allergy and Immunology as: A medical specialty concerned with the hypersensitivity of the individual to foreign substances and protection from the resultant infection or disorder.

nodes.label: Anesthesiology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Anesthesiology as: A specialty concerned with the study of anesthetics and anesthesia.

nodes.label: Bariatric Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Bariatric Medicine as: The discipline concerned with WEIGHT REDUCTION in patients with OBESITY .

nodes.label: Behavioral Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Behavioral Medicine as: The interdisciplinary field concerned with the development and integration of behavioral and biomedical science, knowledge, and techniques relevant to health and illness and the application of this knowledge and these techniques to prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation.

nodes.label: Clinical Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Clinical Medicine as: The study and practice of medicine by direct examination of the patient.

nodes.label: Community Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Community Medicine as: A branch of medicine concerned with the total health of the individual within the home environment and in the community, and with the application of comprehensive care to the prevention and treatment of illness in the entire community.

nodes.label: Disaster Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Disaster Medicine as: Branch of medicine involved with management and organization of public health response to disasters and major events including the special health and medical needs of a community in a disaster.

nodes.label: Emergency Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Emergency Medicine as: The branch of medicine concerned with the evaluation and initial treatment of urgent and emergent medical problems, such as those caused by accidents, trauma, sudden illness, poisoning, or disasters. Emergency medical care can be provided at the hospital or at sites outside the medical facility.

nodes.label: Forensic Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Medicine as: The application of medical knowledge to questions of law.

nodes.label: Functional Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Functional Medicine as: The clinical application of SYSTEMS BIOLOGY , that focuses on identifying the underlying drivers of a patient's disease and addressing, through personalized therapeutic interventions, those root causes of the disease.

nodes.label: General Practice
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes General Practice as: Patient-based medical care provided across age and gender or specialty boundaries.

nodes.label: Genetics, Medical
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Genetics, Medical as: A subdiscipline of human genetics which entails the reliable prediction of certain human disorders as a function of the lineage and/or genetic makeup of an individual or of any two parents or potential parents.

nodes.label: Geography, Medical
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Geography, Medical as: The area of medicine concerned with the effects on health and disease due to geographic factors such as CLIMATE , environmental conditions, and geographic location.

nodes.label: Geriatrics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Geriatrics as: The branch of medicine concerned with the physiological and pathological aspects of the aged, including the clinical problems of senescence and senility.

nodes.label: Global Health
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Global Health as: A multi- and interdisciplinary field concerned with improving health and achieving equity in health for all people. It transcends national boundaries, promotes cooperation and collaboration within and beyond health science fields, and combines population-based disease prevention with individually-based patient care.

nodes.label: Hospital Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Hospital Medicine as: The branch of medicine concerned with the delivery of comprehensive medical care to hospitalized patients. Practitioners include physicians and non-physician providers who engage in clinical care, teaching, research, or leadership in the field of general hospital medicine.(from http://www.hospitalmedicine.org/AM/Template.cfm?Section=Hospitalist_Definition)

nodes.label: Integrative Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Integrative Medicine as: The discipline concerned with using the combination of conventional allopathic medicine and ALTERNATIVE MEDICINE to address the biological, psychological, social, and spiritual aspects of health and illness.

nodes.label: Internal Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Internal Medicine as: A medical specialty concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the internal organ systems of adults.

nodes.label: Military Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Military Medicine as: The practice of medicine as applied to special circumstances associated with military operations.

nodes.label: Molecular Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Molecular Medicine as: The field of medicine concerned with understanding the biochemical basis of health and disease and involved in developing diagnostic and therapeutic methods that utilize MOLECULAR BIOLOGY techniques.

nodes.label: Naval Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Naval Medicine as: The practice of medicine concerned with conditions affecting the health of individuals associated with the marine environment.

nodes.label: Osteopathic Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Osteopathic Medicine as: A medical discipline that is based on the philosophy that all body systems are interrelated and dependent upon one another for good health. This philosophy, developed in 1874 by Dr. Andrew Taylor Still, recognizes the concept of wellness and the importance of treating illness within the context of the whole body. Special attention is placed on the MUSCULOSKELETAL SYSTEM .

nodes.label: Palliative Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Palliative Medicine as: A branch of medicine concerned with preventing and relieving the suffering of patients in any stage of disease. Its focus is on comprehensive care and improving the quality of all areas of the patient's life.

nodes.label: Pediatrics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Pediatrics as: A medical specialty concerned with maintaining health and providing medical care to children from birth to adolescence.

nodes.label: Perioperative Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Perioperative Medicine as: A medical specialty concerned with the patient before and after surgical procedures.

nodes.label: Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Physical and Rehabilitation Medicine as: A medical specialty concerned with the use of physical agents, mechanical apparatus, and manipulation in rehabilitating physically diseased or injured patients.

nodes.label: Psychiatry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Psychiatry as: The medical science that deals with the origin, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of mental disorders.

nodes.label: Public Health
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Public Health as: Branch of medicine concerned with the prevention and control of disease and disability, and the promotion of physical and mental health of the population on the international, national, state, or municipal level.

nodes.label: Regenerative Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Regenerative Medicine as: A field of medicine concerned with developing and using strategies aimed at repair or replacement of damaged, diseased, or metabolically deficient organs, tissues, and cells via TISSUE ENGINEERING ; CELL TRANSPLANTATION ; and ARTIFICIAL ORGANS and BIOARTIFICIAL ORGANS and tissues.

nodes.label: Reproductive Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Reproductive Medicine as: A medical-surgical specialty concerned with the morphology, physiology, biochemistry, and pathology of reproduction in man and other animals, and on the biological, medical, and veterinary problems of fertility and lactation. It includes ovulation induction, diagnosis of infertility and recurrent pregnancy loss, and assisted reproductive technologies such as embryo transfer, in vitro fertilization, and intrafallopian transfer of zygotes. (From Infertility and Reproductive Medicine Clinics of North America, Foreword 1990; Journal of Reproduction and Fertility, Notice to Contributors, Jan 1979)

nodes.label: Social Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Social Medicine as: A branch of medicine concerned with the role of socio-environmental factors in the occurrence, prevention and treatment of disease.

nodes.label: Specialties, Surgical
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Specialties, Surgical as: Various branches of surgical practice limited to specialized areas.

nodes.label: Sports Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Sports Medicine as: The field of medicine concerned with physical fitness and the diagnosis and treatment of injuries sustained in exercise and sports activities.

nodes.label: Theranostic Nanomedicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Theranostic Nanomedicine as: An integrated nano-scale approach to MEDICINE which involves concurrent diagnosis, drug delivery, therapy, and monitoring of therapeutic response.

nodes.label: Travel Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Travel Medicine as: Multidisciplinary field focusing on prevention of infectious diseases and patient safety during international TRAVEL . Key element of patient's pre-travel visit to the physician is a health risk assessment.

nodes.label: Tropical Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Tropical Medicine as: The branch of medicine concerned with diseases, mainly of parasitic origin, common in tropical and subtropical regions.

nodes.label: Vaccinology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Vaccinology as: Branch of medicine concerned with the development of vaccines to control disease by identifying genetic and other mechanisms and pathways that determine immune responses, and thereby provide new candidate vaccine approaches.

nodes.label: Venereology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Venereology as: A branch of medicine which deals with sexually transmitted disease.

nodes.label: Wilderness Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Wilderness Medicine as: Skills and knowledge required for assessment and treatment of traumatic, environmental, and medical emergencies in remote geographic or wilderness environments.

nodes.label: Immunochemistry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Immunochemistry as: Field of chemistry that pertains to immunological phenomena and the study of chemical reactions related to antigen stimulation of tissues. It includes physicochemical interactions between antigens and antibodies.

nodes.label: Immunoinformatics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Immunoinformatics as: The interface between INFORMATICS and IMMUNOLOGY . Otherwise known as computational immunology, it is the use of computational methods and resources for studying IMMUNE SYSTEM PHENOMENA .

nodes.label: Evidence-Based Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Evidence-Based Medicine as: An approach of practicing medicine with the goal to improve and evaluate patient care. It requires the judicious integration of best research evidence with the patient's values to make decisions about medical care. This method is to help physicians make proper diagnosis, devise best testing plan, choose best treatment and methods of disease prevention, as well as develop guidelines for large groups of patients with the same disease. (from JAMA 296 (9), 2006)

nodes.label: Genomic Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Genomic Medicine as: A medical discipline using genomic information about an individual as part of their clinical care (e.g. for diagnostic or therapeutic decision-making) and the health outcomes and policy implications of that clinical use. (From www.genome.gov/health/Genomics-and-Medicine accessed 12/28/2020)

nodes.label: Precision Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Precision Medicine as: Clinical, therapeutic and diagnostic approaches to optimal disease management based on individual variations in a patient's genetic profile.

nodes.label: Pediatric Emergency Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Pediatric Emergency Medicine as: Branch of EMERGENCY MEDICINE dealing with the emergency care of children.

nodes.label: Forensic Genetics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Genetics as: The application of genetic analyses and MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTIC TECHNIQUES to legal matters and crime analysis.

nodes.label: Forensic Pathology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Pathology as: The application of pathology to questions of law.

nodes.label: Family Practice
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Family Practice as: A medical specialty concerned with the provision of continuing, comprehensive primary health care for the entire family.

nodes.label: Topography, Medical
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Topography, Medical as: The systematic surveying, mapping, charting, and description of specific geographical sites, with reference to the physical features that were presumed to influence health and disease. Medical topography should be differentiated from EPIDEMIOLOGY in that the former emphasizes geography whereas the latter emphasizes disease outbreaks.

nodes.label: Geroscience
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Geroscience as: The study of the BIOLOGY ; BIOCHEMISTRY ; and PHYSIOLOGY of AGING and the AGED and age-related diseases such as CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES ; DIABETES MELLITUS ; and CANCER , as well as debilitating conditions like ARTHRITIS ; FATIGUE ; and FRAILTY .

nodes.label: Infectious Disease Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Infectious Disease Medicine as: A branch of internal medicine concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of INFECTIOUS DISEASES .

nodes.label: Medical Oncology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Medical Oncology as: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of neoplasms.

nodes.label: Pulmonary Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Pulmonary Medicine as: A subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of the RESPIRATORY SYSTEM . It is especially concerned with diagnosis and treatment of diseases and defects of the lungs and bronchial tree.

nodes.label: Sleep Medicine Specialty
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Sleep Medicine Specialty as: A medical specialty concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of SLEEP WAKE DISORDERS and their causes.

nodes.label: Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Diving and Hyperbaric Medicine as: The practice of medicine concerned with conditions in individuals resulting from exposure to environments where the ambient pressure is increased, such as the undersea environment.

nodes.label: Submarine Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Submarine Medicine as: The field of medicine concerned with conditions affecting the health of people in submarines or sealabs.

nodes.label: Neurotology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Neurotology as: A subspecialty of otolaryngology dealing with the parts of the nervous system related to the ear.

nodes.label: Pathology, Clinical
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Pathology, Clinical as: A subspecialty of pathology applied to the solution of clinical problems, especially the use of laboratory methods in clinical diagnosis. (Dorland, 28th ed.)

nodes.label: Pathology, Molecular
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Pathology, Molecular as: A subspecialty of pathology concerned with the molecular basis (e.g., mutations) of various diseases.

nodes.label: Pathology, Surgical
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Pathology, Surgical as: A field of anatomical pathology in which living tissue is surgically removed for the purpose of diagnosis and treatment.

nodes.label: Perinatology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Perinatology as: The branch of medicine dealing with the FETUS and NEWBORN during the perinatal period. The perinatal period begins with the twenty-eighth week of gestation and ends twenty-eight days after birth.

nodes.label: Adolescent Psychiatry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Adolescent Psychiatry as: The medical science that deals with the origin, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of mental disorders in individuals 13-18 years.

nodes.label: Biological Psychiatry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Biological Psychiatry as: An interdisciplinary science concerned with studies of the biological bases of behavior - biochemical, genetic, physiological, and neurological - and applying these to the understanding and treatment of mental illness.

nodes.label: Child Psychiatry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Child Psychiatry as: The medical science that deals with the origin, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of mental disorders in children.

nodes.label: Community Psychiatry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Community Psychiatry as: Branch of psychiatry concerned with the provision and delivery of a coordinated program of mental health care to a specified population. The foci included in this concept are: all social, psychological and physical factors related to etiology, prevention, and maintaining positive mental health in the community.

nodes.label: Forensic Psychiatry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Psychiatry as: Psychiatry in its legal aspects. This includes criminology, penology, COMMITMENT OF PERSONS WITH PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS , the psychiatrist's role in compensation cases, the problems of releasing information to the court, and of expert testimony.

nodes.label: Geriatric Psychiatry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Geriatric Psychiatry as: A subspecialty of psychiatry concerned with the mental health of the aged.

nodes.label: Military Psychiatry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Military Psychiatry as: Branch of psychiatry concerned with problems related to the prevention, diagnosis, etiology, and treatment of mental or emotional disorders of Armed Forces personnel.

nodes.label: Neuropsychiatry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Neuropsychiatry as: A subfield of psychiatry that emphasizes the somatic substructure on which mental operations and emotions are based, and the functional or organic disturbances of the central nervous system that give rise to, contribute to, or are associated with mental and emotional disorders. (From Campbell's Psychiatric Dictionary, 8th ed.)

nodes.label: Preventive Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Preventive Medicine as: A medical specialty primarily concerned with prevention of disease ( PRIMARY PREVENTION ) and the promotion and preservation of health in the individual.

nodes.label: Nuclear Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Nuclear Medicine as: A specialty field of radiology concerned with diagnostic, therapeutic, and investigative use of radioactive compounds.

nodes.label: Radiation Oncology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Radiation Oncology as: A subspecialty of medical oncology and radiology concerned with the radiotherapy of cancer.

nodes.label: Imaging Genomics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Imaging Genomics as: The field of study investigating the relationship between imaging features, identified during various imaging procedures, and the presence of various genetic or molecular markers of particular disorders and diseases.

nodes.label: Radiation Genomics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Radiation Genomics as: The study of the association between patient genomic data and the response to IONIZING RADIATION .

nodes.label: Radiology, Interventional
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Radiology, Interventional as: Subspecialty of radiology that combines organ system radiography, catheter techniques and sectional imaging.

nodes.label: Acute Care Surgery
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Acute Care Surgery as: Surgical specialty generally encompassing emergency general surgery, surgical critical care and trauma care. Acute care surgery is a component of general surgery related to care of patients with acute, life-threatening or potentially life-threatening surgical conditions.

nodes.label: Colorectal Surgery
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Colorectal Surgery as: A surgical specialty concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of disorders and abnormalities of the COLON ; RECTUM ; and ANAL CANAL .

nodes.label: General Surgery
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes General Surgery as: A specialty in which manual or operative procedures are used in the treatment of disease, injuries, or deformities.

nodes.label: Neurosurgery
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Neurosurgery as: A surgical specialty concerned with the treatment of diseases and disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and peripheral and sympathetic nervous system.

nodes.label: Obstetrics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Obstetrics as: A medical-surgical specialty concerned with management and care of women during pregnancy, parturition, and the puerperium.

nodes.label: Orthognathic Surgery
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Orthognathic Surgery as: A surgical specialty concerned with correcting conditions related to malposition of the jawbones and other related MAXILLOFACIAL ABNORMALITIES (e.g., CLEFT PALATE ; RETROGNATHISM ).

nodes.label: Orthopedics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Orthopedics as: A specialty which utilizes medical, surgical, and physical methods to treat and correct deformities, diseases, and injuries to the skeletal system, its articulations, and associated structures.

nodes.label: Otolaryngology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Otolaryngology as: A surgical specialty concerned with the study and treatment of disorders of the ear, nose, and throat.

nodes.label: Surgery, Plastic
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Surgery, Plastic as: The branch of surgery concerned with restoration, reconstruction, or improvement of defective, damaged, or missing structures.

nodes.label: Surgical Oncology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Surgical Oncology as: A surgical specialty concerned with management of cancer.

nodes.label: Thoracic Surgery
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Thoracic Surgery as: A surgical specialty concerned with diagnosis and treatment of disorders of the heart, lungs, and esophagus. Two major types of thoracic surgery are classified as pulmonary and cardiovascular.

nodes.label: Sports Nutritional Sciences
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Sports Nutritional Sciences as: The study of NUTRITION PROCESSES during EXERCISE and ATHLETIC PERFORMANCE as well as specific NUTRITIONAL REQUIREMENTS of ATHLETES and the relationship between NUTRITIONAL STATUS and NUTRITION DISORDERS in athletes.

nodes.label: Veterinary Sports Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Veterinary Sports Medicine as: The field of veterinary medicine concerned with PHYSICAL FITNESS of animals in sports (horse racing, dog racing, etc.) and the diagnosis and treatment of sports injuries in animals.

nodes.label: Evidence-Based Emergency Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Evidence-Based Emergency Medicine as: A way of providing emergency medical care that is guided by a thoughtful integration of the best available scientific knowledge with clinical expertise in EMERGENCY MEDICINE . This approach allows the practitioner to critically assess research data, clinical guidelines, and other information resources in order to correctly identify the clinical problem, apply the most high-quality intervention, and re-evaluate the outcome for future improvement.

nodes.label: Cardiac Electrophysiology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Cardiac Electrophysiology as: The study of the electrical activity and characteristics of the HEART ; MYOCARDIUM ; and CARDIOMYOCYTES .

nodes.label: Cardio-Oncology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Cardio-Oncology as: The study, diagnosis, and treatment of CARDIOTOXICITY in patients who undergo treatment for cancer.

nodes.label: Transfusion Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Transfusion Medicine as: The area of hematology that is concerned with the transfusion of blood and blood components, and in prevention and treatment of adverse effects from BLOOD TRANSFUSION errors.

nodes.label: Psycho-Oncology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Psycho-Oncology as: A specialty which deals with the interrelationship of physical, psychological, social, behavioral, and ethical aspects of cancer. Psycho-oncology examines the behavioral and psychosocial factors that may influence the course of the disease, cancer risk, prevention, and detection.

nodes.label: Preventive Psychiatry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Preventive Psychiatry as: A discipline concerned with the prevention of mental illness and the promotion of mental health.

nodes.label: Molecular Epidemiology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Molecular Epidemiology as: The application of molecular biology to the answering of epidemiological questions. The examination of patterns of changes in DNA to implicate particular carcinogens and the use of molecular markers to predict which individuals are at highest risk for a disease are common examples.

nodes.label: Pharmacoepidemiology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Pharmacoepidemiology as: The science concerned with the benefit and risk of drugs used in populations and the analysis of the outcomes of drug therapies. Pharmacoepidemiologic data come from both clinical trials and epidemiological studies with emphasis on methods for the detection and evaluation of drug-related adverse effects, assessment of risk vs benefit ratios in drug therapy, patterns of drug utilization, the cost-effectiveness of specific drugs, methodology of postmarketing surveillance, and the relation between pharmacoepidemiology and the formulation and interpretation of regulatory guidelines. (Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf 1992;1(1); J Pharmacoepidemiol 1990;1(1))

nodes.label: Earth sciences
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Earth sciences as: Broad term for all science related to the study of the earth. This category is also used for geosciences

nodes.label: Geologic time periods
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Geologic time periods as: This category is also used for geologic age and geologic time

nodes.label: Hazards
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Hazards as: Potential dangers from both natural processes (e.g., earthquakes, floods, and climate change) and human impacts on the environment. This category is also used for catastrophes , with coastal processes for coastal hazards , disasters , with earthquakes for earthquake hazards , emergency management resources , environmental hazards , geologic hazards , with algal blooms for harmful algal blooms , and with ocean processes for ocean hazards

nodes.label: Earth characteristics
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Earth characteristics as: The measurable, definable properties and features of the earth.

nodes.label: Atmospheric sciences
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Atmospheric sciences as: Studies relating to composition, structure, physics, chemistry, and dynamics of the atmosphere.

nodes.label: Geography
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Geography as: Study of the earth's landforms, topography, and climate, the distribution of flora and fauna, and the distribution, culture, and activities of human populations. This category is also used for geographic information sciences

nodes.label: Geophysics
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Geophysics as: Branch of geology studying the physical characteristics and phenomena of the earth and its atmosphere. This category is also used with maps and atlases for geophysical maps

nodes.label: Ocean sciences
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ocean sciences as: Sciences involved in the study of geological, biological, chemical, and physical characteristics and processes of the oceans. This category is also used for oceanography and physical oceanography

nodes.label: Soil sciences
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Soil sciences as: Earth sciences dealing with the origin, classification, physical, chemical, and biological properties of soils. This category is also used for pedology (soils)

nodes.label: Phanerozoic
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Phanerozoic as: Eon of geologic time approximately 542 million years ago extending to the present. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Precambrian
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Precambrian as: General interval of geologic time before approximately 542 million years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059 This category is also used for cryptozoic

nodes.label: Atmospheric properties
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Atmospheric properties as: Characteristics of the mass of gases surrounding the earth such as composition, temperature, pressure, and humidity. This category is also used for atmosphere properties

nodes.label: Earth material properties
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Earth material properties as: Physical characteristics of rocks and unconsolidated earth materials such as soils and sediments.

nodes.label: Earth structure
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Earth structure as: Major interior structural features of the planet earth.

nodes.label: Geologic history
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Geologic history as: Record (and inferred reconstruction) of the origin and development of the earth since its formation. This category is also used for chronostratigraphy and geohistory

nodes.label: Geologic structure
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Geologic structure as: General position of rocks in an area, and geometrical relationships among rocks.

nodes.label: Gravitational field (earth)
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Gravitational field (earth) as: Region or space around earth's mass which exerts a force that mutually attracts other masses in proportion to the product of the two masses and the distance between them. This category is also used for gravity , with maps and atlases for gravity anomaly maps , and gravity field

nodes.label: Lakebed characteristics
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Lakebed characteristics as: Characteristics of the bottom of inland bodies of water. This category is also used for lake-bed characteristics , lake-bottom characteristics , and lake-floor characteristics

nodes.label: Land surface characteristics
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Land surface characteristics as: Features and attributes of earth's land surface. This category is also used for landscape and physiography

nodes.label: Magnetic field (earth)
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Magnetic field (earth) as: The magnetic region surrounding earth. It is generated by the dipolar characteristic of earth's core whereby earth itself acts as a great spherical magnet with poles near, but not exactly at, the North and South poles. This category is also used for geomagnetic field , geomagnetics , geomagnetism , with maps and atlases for magnetic anomaly maps , magnetic field , and magnetosphere

nodes.label: Ocean characteristics
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ocean characteristics as: The attributes and process of seas and oceans. This category is also used for ocean mixed-layer depth , with field inventory and monitoring for ocean monitoring , ocean surface characteristics , with ocean processes for oceans , and sea surface reflectance

nodes.label: Rocks and deposits
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Rocks and deposits as: Solid masses that make up the earth's crust as well as accumulations of materials. Use for major rock types and unconsolidated deposits. For deposits of economic value, see related terms. This category is also used for crystals , with maps and atlases for lithologic maps , lithology , and rock composition

nodes.label: Snow and ice cover
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Snow and ice cover as: Accumulation of snow or ice blanketing land surfaces. This category is also used for cryosphere , glaciers , ice , with drilling and coring for ice core sampling , and snowpack

nodes.label: Stratigraphic sections
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Stratigraphic sections as: Vertical arrangement in layers of rock units whose sequence is used to study the geological history of the strata. This category is also used for geologic sections , geologic units , sections (geologic) , sections (stratigraphic) , strata , and stratum

nodes.label: Topography
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Topography as: Configuration of the land surface and sea floor. This category is also used for elevation and relief

nodes.label: Soil chemistry
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Soil chemistry as: Branch of chemistry concerned with the elements and compounds that make up soils. Includes chemical processes involving soils.

nodes.label: Water chemistry
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Water chemistry as: Branch of chemistry that deals with the elements and compounds in water.

nodes.label: Paleogeography
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Paleogeography as: Study of the history of earth surface characteristics; geomorphology in the past.

nodes.label: Economic geology
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Economic geology as: Scientific study of the formation, location, and use of marketable geologic materials including fuels, metals, minerals, and water.

nodes.label: Marine geology
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Marine geology as: Branch of geology concerned with the composition, geologic history, and earth processes of the ocean floor and the continental margin. This category is also used for geological oceanography

nodes.label: Structural geology
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Structural geology as: Branch of geology concerned with the distribution, position, shape, and internal structure of rocks.

nodes.label: Geodesy
