nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Geodesy as: Branch of science dealing with measuring the earth or large areas of the earth for making maps, determining the size and shape of the earth, and correlating gravitational, geological, and magnetic surveys of the earth.

nodes.label: Marine geophysics
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Marine geophysics as: Branch of earth sciences concerned with the physical processes of the oceans and continental margins. We include here studies of large bodies of brackish and fresh water, such as lakes and rivers.

nodes.label: Hydrodynamics
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Hydrodynamics as: Principles of fluid dynamics applied to water bodies. This category is also used for fluid dynamics

nodes.label: Paleoceanography
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Paleoceanography as: Study of the oceans in the geologic past, including their physical, chemical, biologic, and geologic history.

nodes.label: Invertebrate paleontology
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Invertebrate paleontology as: Branch of paleontology which deals with fossil animals without backbones.

nodes.label: Micropaleontology
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Micropaleontology as: Branch of paleontology dealing with fossils too small to be seen without a microscope.

nodes.label: Paleobotany
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Paleobotany as: Branch of paleontology concerned with the study of fossil plants and plant life in the geologic past.

nodes.label: Vertebrate paleontology
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Vertebrate paleontology as: Branch of paleontology dealing with fossil animals that have spinal columns.

nodes.label: Cenozoic
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Cenozoic as: Era of geologic time approximately 65 million years ago extending to the present. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Mesozoic
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Mesozoic as: Era of geologic time approximately 251 to 65 million years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Paleozoic
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Paleozoic as: Era of geologic time approximately 542 to 251 million years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Archaean
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Archaean as: Eon of geologic time approximately 4 to 2.5 billion years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Hadean
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Hadean as: Eon of geologic time prior to 4 billion years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Proterozoic
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Proterozoic as: Eon of geologic time approximately 2.5 billion to 542 million years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Air temperature
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Air temperature as: This category is also used for temperature (air)

nodes.label: Atmospheric composition
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Atmospheric composition as: Components of the mass of gases that surrounds a planet. The earth's atmosphere consists of nitrogen, oxygen, and small portions of other gases. This category is also used with contamination and pollution for air pollution

nodes.label: Acid neutralizing potential
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Acid neutralizing potential as: Geochemical capacity of earth materials to affect the pH of waters flowing through them. This category is also used for acid neutralizing capacity and neutralization potential

nodes.label: Bulk density
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Bulk density as: Overall density of an unconsolidated earth material.

nodes.label: Electromagnetic reflectance and emissivity
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Electromagnetic reflectance and emissivity as: Effectiveness of an earth material in reflecting or emitting radiation, varying by wavelength. Measurements are made over the infrared part of the electromagnetic spectrum in a laboratory to compare with remotely-sensed data obtained by airborne or satellite imaging systems. This category is also used for infrared reflectance , laboratory reflectance , laboratory spectra , spectral radiance , and spectral reflectance

nodes.label: Magnetism
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Magnetism as: Strength and orientation of the permanent magnetic field in a given sample of an earth material

nodes.label: Permeability
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Permeability as: The ability of fluids to pass through an earth material, typically depending on the connectedness of pore space in the material. This category is also used for soil permeability

nodes.label: Porosity
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Porosity as: The proportion of open space in a rock or unconsolidated material. This category is also used for interstices and soil porosity

nodes.label: Radioactivity
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Radioactivity as: Release of subatomic particles from earth materials. Generally the energy of these particles is used to determine the chemical elements present. This category is also used for gamma ray emission

nodes.label: Resistivity
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Resistivity as: Electrical resistance of materials, often measured in boreholes.

nodes.label: Soil moisture
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Soil moisture as: Water content of soil and other near-surface unconsolidated earth material

nodes.label: Soil temperature
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Soil temperature as: Temperature and temperature gradients in soil and other near-surface unconsolidated earth materials

nodes.label: Core (earth)
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Core (earth) as: The superdense center of the earth composed of two layers: a liquid outer layer and a solid inner core of metallic iron-nickel alloy.

nodes.label: Crust (earth)
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Crust (earth) as: The outermost layer of the earth which is relatively thin, of lower density than the core, and rocky.

nodes.label: Mantle (earth)
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Mantle (earth) as: Zone of earth's interior between the crust and the core. It is 2,900 kilometers (1,740 miles) thick and consists of a dense upper layer (upper mantle) and a partially molten lower layer (lower mantle), separated by a transition zone.

nodes.label: Earth history
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Earth history as: The structural and compositional changes that the earth has undergone from its formation. Use for discussions of the whole earth (or large sections of it) instead of regional studies.

nodes.label: Foliation (geologic)
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Foliation (geologic) as: The property of rocks or glaciers splitting into thin layers or plates due to the orientation of crystals and dynamic movement.

nodes.label: Lineation (geologic)
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Lineation (geologic) as: Linear topographic feature on the earth's surface or in rocks. This category is also used for lineaments

nodes.label: Structure contours
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Structure contours as: Gridding and contouring lines drawn on geologic maps to depict boundaries of structural features. This category is also used with maps and atlases for depth-to maps

nodes.label: Bouguer anomaly
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Bouguer anomaly as: Gravity anomaly corrected to remove the effects of topography using knowledge of the terrain in the area surrounding the measurement station.

nodes.label: Free-air anomaly
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Free-air anomaly as: Gravity anomaly corrected for elevation of the location at which the measurements were made.

nodes.label: Gravity gradient
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Gravity gradient as: Lateral variation of the three-dimensional vector components of gravity, typically measured using airborne sensors. This category is also used for gravity gradiometry

nodes.label: Isostatic anomaly
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Isostatic anomaly as: Gravity anomaly corrected for the effects of low-density rocks underlying mountains.

nodes.label: Lakebed acoustic reflectivity
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Lakebed acoustic reflectivity as: Acoustic energy received by a sonar system, providing a measure of the roughness of the lakebed. This category is also used for backscatter (lakebed)

nodes.label: Karst
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Karst as: Landscape characterized by dissolution features in carbonate or evaporite terranes, often containing caves and sinkholes. This category is also used for karst topography and karstic

nodes.label: Ocean salinity
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ocean salinity as: Measure of the percentage of dissolved salts in seawater.

nodes.label: Ocean temperature
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Ocean temperature as: Distribution of heat in the oceans, including surface water, thermocline and mode waters, and deep waters. Includes discussion and measures of both in-situ and potential temperature. This category is also used for temperature (ocean)

nodes.label: Sea-floor characteristics
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Sea-floor characteristics as: Geomorphic features and geographic, compositional, and textural variation in the materials composing the ocean floor. Includes both large-scale structures (such as seamounts and rises) and fine-scale variations in rocks and deposits on the sea floor. This category is also used for ocean bottom characteristics , sea floor characteristics , and seafloor characteristics

nodes.label: Sea-level change
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Sea-level change as: Variation in the relative vertical position of land and ocean waters. Caused globally by changes in the distribution of ice masses and the shape of the oceans, and locally by the rate of uplift or subsidence of the land surface. Includes both global (eustatic) and local (relative) sea-level variations. This category is also used for sea level change , sea level rise , and sea-level rise

nodes.label: Fossils
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Fossils as: Recognizable remains such as bones, shells, leaves, burrows, impressions, or tracks of past life on the earth. This category is also used for index fossils and microfossils

nodes.label: Igneous rocks
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Igneous rocks as: Rocks formed from melted rock that has cooled and solidified.

nodes.label: Metamorphic rocks
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Metamorphic rocks as: Sedimentary or igneous rocks which have undergone such intense changes in temperature, pressure, structural stress, or chemical environment that they are transformed into denser rocks.

nodes.label: Mineral deposits
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Mineral deposits as: Deposits in which particular minerals are concentrated, typically noticed and studied if the minerals have economic value. This category is also used for ore deposits

nodes.label: Permafrost
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Permafrost as: Rocks and deposits in which the interstitial waters remain perennially frozen.

nodes.label: Petroleum
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Petroleum as: Naturally occurring hydrocarbons, typically fluid or gas, often of economic use. Includes oil, natural gas, and asphaltic compounds found in tar sands and oil shales. This category is also used with industrial pollution for oil spills

nodes.label: Sedimentary rocks
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Sedimentary rocks as: Rocks formed by the consolidation of loose, uncemented pieces of sediments.

nodes.label: Unconsolidated deposits
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Unconsolidated deposits as: Loosely bound sediments such as sand, gravel, and silt which tend to accumulate in low areas or valleys. This category is also used for alluvium , eolian sediments , loess , with chemical analysis for sediment geochemistry , sediments , and surficial deposits

nodes.label: Sea ice concentration
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Sea ice concentration as: Proportion of ocean area in a given region that contains or is covered by floating ice. This category is also used for sea ice cover and sea-ice concentration

nodes.label: Bedrock geologic units
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Bedrock geologic units as: Units of consolidated (solid) rock that underlie soils or other unconsolidated materials. This category is also used with maps and atlases for basement maps and geologic formations

nodes.label: Geologic contacts
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Geologic contacts as: Junctions of two different rock formations varying by type or age of rock, including faults, unconformities, and bedding planes. This category is also used for contacts (geologic)

nodes.label: Stratigraphic thickness
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Stratigraphic thickness as: Thickness of earth material layers or groups of such layers, often portrayed as isopachs (contours) or gridded data. This category is also used for isopach , with maps and atlases for isopach maps , sediment thickness , and with maps and atlases for stratigraphic thickness maps

nodes.label: Surficial geologic units
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Surficial geologic units as: Rock units on the earth's surface. This category is also used with maps and atlases for surficial geologic maps

nodes.label: Bathymetry
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Bathymetry as: The elevation of the earth's surface beneath a body of water, especially the ocean, typically determined by measurements of depth from the water surface. This category is also used for bathymetry data , sea floor topography , and underwater contours

nodes.label: Marine chemistry
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Marine chemistry as: Branch of chemistry that deals with the properties, composition, structure, and interaction of substances in the seas and oceans. This category is also used for chemical oceanography , ocean chemistry , and water properties (marine)

nodes.label: Biostratigraphy
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Biostratigraphy as: Branch of geology concerned with the separation and differentiation of rock units based on the fossils they contain.

nodes.label: Lithostratigraphy
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Lithostratigraphy as: Branch of stratigraphy dealing with the study of units of rock. Each unit is composed of a body of rock which is dominated by a certain lithology or similar color, mineralogic composition, and grain size.

nodes.label: Paleoseismology
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Paleoseismology as: Branch of seismology concerned with ancient earthquakes. Clues which indicate seismic activities in the geologic past are used to date and determine the effects of those earthquakes.

nodes.label: Quaternary
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Quaternary as: Period of geologic time approximately 2.6 million years ago extending to the present. In new studies, this term is deprecated in favor of Holocene and Pleistocene. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Tertiary
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Tertiary as: Period of geologic time approximately 65 to 1.8 million years ago. In new studies, this term is deprecated in favor of Neogene and Paleogene. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Cretaceous
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Cretaceous as: Period of geologic time approximately 145 to 65 million years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Jurassic
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Jurassic as: Period of geologic time approximately 200 to 145 million years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Triassic
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Triassic as: Period of geologic time approximately 251 to 200 million years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Cambrian
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Cambrian as: Period of geologic time approximately 542 to 488 million years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Devonian
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Devonian as: Period of geologic time approximately 416 to 359 million years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059

nodes.label: Mississippian
nodes.summary: The USGS Thesaurus defines Mississippian as: Subperiod of geologic time approximately 359 to 318 million years ago. https://doi.org/10.3133/fs20103059 This category is also used for lower carboniferous

nodes.label: Humanities
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Humanities as: Fields of inquiry in human constructs and concerns as opposed to natural processes and social relations. These are traditionally the study of literature, philosophy, and religion.

nodes.label: Art
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Art as: Processes and results of aesthetic expression.

nodes.label: Ethical Dilemmas
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethical Dilemmas as: Situations in which two moral principles conflict with one another. Fictional or hypothetical dilemmas of this kind are used to assess the moral beliefs or moral reasoning skills of individuals. (From APA Dictionary of Psychology, https://dictionary.apa.org/)

nodes.label: History
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes History as: Record and study of past events.

nodes.label: Knowledge
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Knowledge as: The body of truths or facts accumulated in the course of time, the cumulated sum of information, its volume and nature, in any civilization, period, or country.

nodes.label: Literature
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Literature as: Writings having excellence of form or expression and expressing ideas of permanent or universal interest. The body of written works produced in a particular language, country, or age. (Webster, 3d ed)

nodes.label: Music
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Music as: Sound that expresses emotion through rhythm, melody, and harmony.

nodes.label: Nature
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Nature as: The system of all phenomena in space and time; the totality of physical reality. It is both a scientific and philosophic concept appearing in all historic eras. (Webster 2d; Dr. James H. Cassedy, NLM History of Medicine Division)

nodes.label: Occultism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Occultism as: The belief in or study of practices and knowledge of magical, mystical, or supernatural powers. ALCHEMY , astrology, and many RELIGIOUS PHILOSOPHIES are based upon occult principles.

nodes.label: Religion
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Religion as: A set of beliefs concerning the nature, cause, and purpose of the universe, especially when considered as the creation of a superhuman agency. It usually involves devotional and ritual observances and often a moral code for the conduct of human affairs. (Random House Collegiate Dictionary, rev. ed.)

nodes.label: Romanticism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Romanticism as: The attitude or intellectual orientation that characterized many works of literature, painting, music, architecture, criticism, and historiography in Western civilization over a period from the late 18th to the mid-19th century.

nodes.label: Secularism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Secularism as: Indifference to, or rejection of, RELIGION or religious considerations. (From Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed)

nodes.label: Human Body
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Human Body as: The human being as a non-anatomical and non-zoological entity. The emphasis is on the philosophical or artistic treatment of the human being, and includes lay and social attitudes toward the body in history. (From J. Cassedy, NLM History of Medicine Division)

nodes.label: Medical Illustration
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Medical Illustration as: The field which deals with illustrative clarification of biomedical concepts, as in the use of diagrams and drawings. The illustration may be produced by hand, photography, computer, or other electronic or mechanical methods.

nodes.label: Medicine in the Arts
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Medicine in the Arts as: Depiction of medical issues or themes via the arts including visual, oral, or written forms of expression.

nodes.label: Numismatics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Numismatics as: Study of coins, tokens, medals, etc. However, it usually refers to medals pertaining to the history of medicine.

nodes.label: Science in the Arts
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Science in the Arts as: Depiction of scientific issues or themes via the arts including visual, oral, or written forms of expression.

nodes.label: Eugenics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Eugenics as: The attempt to improve the PHENOTYPES of future generations of the human population by fostering the reproduction of those with favorable phenotypes and GENOTYPES and hampering or preventing BREEDING by those with undesirable phenotypes and genotypes. The concept is largely discredited. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

nodes.label: Genealogy and Heraldry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Genealogy and Heraldry as: Descent of a person, family, or group from an ancestor and coats of arms and other armorial bearings associated with an ancestor.

nodes.label: Historiography
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Historiography as: The writing of history; the principles, theory, and history of historical writing; the product of historical writing. (Webster, 3d ed)

nodes.label: History of Dentistry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes History of Dentistry as: Study of past events and development in the field of DENTISTRY .

nodes.label: History of Pharmacy
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes History of Pharmacy as: Study of the origins and development of the field of PHARMACY .

nodes.label: History, Ancient
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes History, Ancient as: The period of history before 500 of the common era.

nodes.label: History, Early Modern 1451-1600
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes History, Early Modern 1451-1600 as: The period of history from 1451 through 1600 of the common era.

nodes.label: History, Medieval
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes History, Medieval as: The period of history from the year 500 through 1450 of the common era.

nodes.label: History, Modern 1601-
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes History, Modern 1601- as: The period of history from 1601 of the common era to the present.

nodes.label: History of Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes History of Medicine as: Study of past events and development in the field of Medicine.

nodes.label: History of Nursing
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes History of Nursing as: Study of past events and development in the field of Nursing.

nodes.label: Natural History
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Natural History as: A former branch of knowledge embracing the study, description, and classification of natural objects (as animals, plants, and minerals) and thus including the modern sciences of zoology, botany, and mineralogy insofar as they existed at that time. In the 17th, 18th, and 19th centuries it was much used for the generalized pursuit of certain areas of science. (Webster, 3d ed; from Dr. James H. Cassedy, NLM History of Medicine Division)

nodes.label: Phrenology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Phrenology as: The study of the conformation of the skull as indicative of mental faculties and traits of character, especially according to the hypothesis of F. J. Gall (1758-1828). (Webster 3d ed)

nodes.label: Symbolism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Symbolism as: A concept that stands for or suggests something else by reason of its relationship, association, convention, or resemblance. The symbolism may be mental or a visible sign or representation. (From Webster, 3d ed)

nodes.label: Bible
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Bible as: The book composed of writings generally accepted by Christians as inspired by God and of divine authority. (Webster, 3d ed)

nodes.label: Drama
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Drama as: A composition in prose or verse presenting in dialogue or pantomime a story involving various characters, usually intended to be acted on a stage and to be regarded as a form of entertainment. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

nodes.label: Folklore
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Folklore as: The common orally transmitted traditions, folktales, festivals, songs, superstitions, and stories of all peoples.

nodes.label: Literature, Medieval
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Literature, Medieval as: Writings originating in the 5th century A.D. through the 15h century.

nodes.label: Literature, Modern
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Literature, Modern as: Writings originating from the 15th century A.D. to the present

nodes.label: Medicine in Literature
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Medicine in Literature as: Written or other literary works whose subject matter is medical or about the profession of medicine and related areas.

nodes.label: Mythology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Mythology as: A body of stories, the origins of which may be unknown or forgotten, that explain practices, beliefs, institutions or natural phenomena. Mythology includes legends and folk tales. It may refer to classical mythology or to a body of modern thought and modern life. (From Webster's 1st ed)

nodes.label: Science in Literature
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Science in Literature as: Literary works whose subject matter is science or about the profession of science and related areas.

nodes.label: Alchemy
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Alchemy as: Form of chemistry concerned with discovering methods for transmuting base metals into gold and with finding an elixir for eternal youth.

nodes.label: Astrology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Astrology as: System of thought regarding forecasting of earthly and human events through the observation and interpretation of the fixed stars and planetary bodies.

nodes.label: Esthetics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Esthetics as: The branch of philosophy dealing with the nature of the beautiful. It includes beauty, esthetic experience, esthetic judgment, esthetic aspects of medicine, etc.

nodes.label: Existentialism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Existentialism as: Philosophy based on the analysis of the individual's existence in the world which holds that human existence cannot be completely described in scientific terms. Existentialism also stresses the freedom and responsibility of the individual as well as the uniqueness of religious and ethical experiences and the analysis of subjective phenomena such as anxiety, guilt, and suffering. (APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

nodes.label: Life
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Life as: The state that distinguishes organisms from inorganic matter, manifested by growth, metabolism, reproduction, and adaptation. It includes the course of existence, the sum of experiences, the mode of existing, or the fact of being. Over the centuries inquiries into the nature of life have crossed the boundaries from philosophy to biology, forensic medicine, anthropology, etc., in creative as well as scientific literature. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed; Dr. James H. Cassedy, NLM History of Medicine Division)

nodes.label: Metaphysics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Metaphysics as: The branch of philosophy that treats of first principles, including ontology (the nature of existence or being) and cosmology (the origin and structure of the universe). (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

nodes.label: Morals
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Morals as: Standards of conduct that distinguish right from wrong.

nodes.label: Philosophy, Dental
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Philosophy, Dental as: The underlying rationale or theoretical basis for the principles of DENTISTRY .

nodes.label: Philosophy, Medical
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Philosophy, Medical as: The underlying rationale or theoretical basis for the principles of MEDICINE .

nodes.label: Philosophy, Nursing
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Philosophy, Nursing as: The underlying rationale or theoretical basis for the principles of NURSING .

nodes.label: Postmodernism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Postmodernism as: A late 20th-century philosophical approach or style of cultural analysis that seeks to reveal the cultural or social construction of concepts conventionally assumed to be natural or universal. (from E.R. DuBose, The Illusion of Trust: Toward a Medical Theological Ethics in the Postmodern Age, Kluwer, 1995)

nodes.label: Qi
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Qi as: The vital life force in the body, supposedly able to be regulated by acupuncture. It corresponds roughly to the Greek pneuma, the Latin spiritus, and the ancient Indian prana. The concept of life-breath or vital energy was formulated as an indication of the awareness of man, originally directed externally toward nature or society but later turned inward to the self or life within. (From Comparison between Concepts of Life-Breath in East and West, 15th International Symposium on the Comparative History of Medicine - East and West, August 26-September 3, 1990, Shizuoka, Japan, pp. ix-x)

nodes.label: Utopias
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Utopias as: Ideal perfection especially in laws, government, and social conditions.

nodes.label: Vitalism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Vitalism as: The metaphysical doctrine that the functions and processes of life are due to a vital principle distinct from physicochemical forces and that the laws of physics and chemistry alone cannot explain life functions and processes. Vitalism is opposed to mechanistic materialism. The belief was that matter was divided into two classes based on behavior with respect to heat: organic and inorganic. Inorganic material could be melted but could always be recovered by removing the heat source. Organic compounds changed form upon heating and could not be recovered by removing the heat source. The proposed explanation for the difference between organic and inorganic compounds was the Vitalism Theory, which stated that inorganic materials did not contain the vital force of life.

nodes.label: Yin-Yang
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Yin-Yang as: In Chinese philosophy and religion, two principles, one negative, dark, and feminine (yin) and one positive, bright, and masculine (yang), from whose interaction all things are produced and all things are dissolved. As a concept the two polar elements referred originally to the shady and sunny sides of a valley or a hill but it developed into the relationship of any contrasting pair: those specified above (female-male, etc.) as well as cold-hot, wet-dry, weak-strong, etc. It is not a distinct system of thought by itself but permeates Chinese life and thought. A balance of yin and yang is essential to health. A deficiency of either principle can manifest as disease. (Encyclopedia Americana)

nodes.label: Anthroposophy
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Anthroposophy as: Knowledge of the nature of man. A spiritual and mystical doctrine that grew out of theosophy and derives mainly from the philosophy of Rudolph Steiner, Austrian social philosopher (1861-1925). (Webster, 3d ed)

nodes.label: Buddhism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Buddhism as: The teaching ascribed to Gautama Buddha (ca. 483 B.C.) holding that suffering is inherent in life and that one can escape it into nirvana by mental and moral self-purification. (Webster, 3d ed)

nodes.label: Christianity
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Christianity as: The religion stemming from the life, teachings, and death of Jesus Christ: the religion that believes in God as the Father Almighty who works redemptively through the Holy Spirit for men's salvation and that affirms Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior who proclaimed to man the gospel of salvation. (From Webster, 3d ed)

nodes.label: Hinduism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Hinduism as: A complex body of social, cultural, and religious beliefs and practices evolved in and largely confined to the Indian subcontinent and marked by a caste system, an outlook tending to view all forms and theories as aspects of one eternal being and truth, and the practice of the way of works, the way of knowledge, or the way of devotion as a means of release from the round of rebirths. (From Webster, 3d ed)

nodes.label: Islam
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Islam as: A monotheistic religion promulgated by the Prophet Mohammed with Allah as the deity.

nodes.label: Judaism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Judaism as: The monotheistic religion of the Jews based on the teachings of the Hebrew Scriptures (Torah).

nodes.label: Religion and Medicine
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Religion and Medicine as: The interrelationship of medicine and religion.

nodes.label: Religion and Psychology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Religion and Psychology as: The interrelationship of psychology and religion.

nodes.label: Religion and Science
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Religion and Science as: The interrelationship of science and religion.

nodes.label: Religion and Sex
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Religion and Sex as: The interrelationship of religion and sexual practices and beliefs.

nodes.label: Religious Missions
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Religious Missions as: Programs or projects established by religious groups or institution to support and provide missionary activities, including sharing faith or providing educational, medical, or other assistance.

nodes.label: Religious Philosophies
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Religious Philosophies as: Sets of beliefs on the nature of the universe or Man.

nodes.label: Anatomy, Artistic
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Anatomy, Artistic as: The study of the structures of organisms for applications in art: drawing, painting, sculpture, illustration, etc.

nodes.label: Metaphor
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Metaphor as: The application of a concept to that which it is not literally the same but which suggests a resemblance and comparison. Medical metaphors were widespread in ancient literature; the description of a sick body was often used by ancient writers to define a critical condition of the State, in which one corrupt part can ruin the entire system. (From Med Secoli Arte Sci, 1990;2(3):abstract 331)

nodes.label: Psychiatry in Literature
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Psychiatry in Literature as: Written or other literary works whose subject matter is related to mental disorders or psychiatry from the lay or practitioner perspective.

nodes.label: Philology, Classical
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Philology, Classical as: The study of ancient Greek and Roman literature, including grammar, etymology, criticism, literary history, and language and linguistic history.

nodes.label: Philology, Oriental
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Philology, Oriental as: The study of literature written in languages of Asia and the Far East, including grammar, etymology, criticism, literary history, and language and linguistic history.

nodes.label: Philology, Romance
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Philology, Romance as: The study of literature written in the Romance languages (French, Spanish, Italian, and others descended from Latin), including grammar, etymology, criticism, literary history, and language and linguistic history.

nodes.label: Beauty
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Beauty as: Characteristics or attributes of persons or things which elicit pleasurable feelings.

nodes.label: Beginning of Human Life
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Beginning of Human Life as: The point at which religious ensoulment or PERSONHOOD is considered to begin.

nodes.label: Value of Life
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Value of Life as: The intrinsic moral worth ascribed to a living being. (Bioethics Thesaurus)

nodes.label: Fuzzy Logic
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Fuzzy Logic as: Approximate, quantitative reasoning that is concerned with the linguistic ambiguity which exists in natural or synthetic language. At its core are variables such as good, bad, and young as well as modifiers such as more, less, and very. These ordinary terms represent fuzzy sets in a particular problem. Fuzzy logic plays a key role in many medical expert systems.

nodes.label: Conscience
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Conscience as: The cognitive and affective processes which constitute an internalized moral governor over an individual's moral conduct.

nodes.label: Ethics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethics as: The philosophy or code pertaining to what is ideal in human character and conduct. Also, the field of study dealing with the principles of morality.

nodes.label: Moral Development
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Moral Development as: The process by which individuals internalize standards of right and wrong conduct.

nodes.label: Social Responsibility
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Social Responsibility as: The obligations and accountability assumed in carrying out actions or ideas on behalf of others.

nodes.label: Virtues
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Virtues as: Character traits that are considered to be morally praiseworthy. (Bioethics Thesaurus)

nodes.label: Ethics, Dental
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethics, Dental as: The principles of proper professional conduct concerning the rights and duties of the dentist, relations with patients and fellow practitioners, as well as actions of the dentist in patient care and interpersonal relations with patient families. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

nodes.label: Empiricism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Empiricism as: One of the principal schools of medical philosophy in ancient Greece and Rome. It developed in Alexandria between 270 and 220 B.C., the only one to have any success in reviving the essentials of the Hippocratic concept. The Empiricists declared that the search for ultimate causes of phenomena was vain, but they were active in endeavoring to discover immediate causes. The tripod of the Empirics was their own chance observations (experience), learning obtained from contemporaries and predecessors (experience of others), and, in the case of new diseases, the formation of conclusions from other diseases which they resembled (analogy). Empiricism enjoyed sporadic continuing popularity in later centuries up to the nineteenth. (From Castiglioni, A History of Medicine, 2d ed, p186; Dr. James H. Cassedy, NLM History of Medicine Division)

nodes.label: Holistic Health
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Holistic Health as: Health as viewed from the perspective that humans function as complete, integrated units rather than as aggregates of separate parts.

nodes.label: Humoralism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Humoralism as: An ancient Greek medical theory that health and illness result from a balance or imbalance of body fluids or humors. The humors are blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.

nodes.label: Hygiene Hypothesis
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Hygiene Hypothesis as: The theory that infectious agents, symbiotic microorganisms, and parasites are normal stimulants for the maturation of the immune system toward a balanced immune response. The theory predicts that lack of such stimulation leads to allergies and AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES .

nodes.label: Ethics, Nursing
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Ethics, Nursing as: The principles of proper professional conduct concerning the rights and duties of nurses themselves, their patients, and their fellow practitioners, as well as their actions in the care of patients and in relations with their families.

nodes.label: Holistic Nursing
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Holistic Nursing as: A philosophy of nursing practice that takes into account total patient care, considering the physical, emotional, social, economic, and spiritual needs of patients, their response to their illnesses, and the effect of illness on patients' abilities to meet self-care needs. (From Mosby's Medical, Nursing, & Allied Health Dictionary, 4th ed, p745)

nodes.label: Catholicism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Catholicism as: The Christian faith, practice, or system of the Catholic Church, specifically the Roman Catholic, the Christian church that is characterized by a hierarchic structure of bishops and priests in which doctrinal and disciplinary authority are dependent upon apostolic succession, with the pope as head of the episcopal college. (From Webster, 3d ed; American Heritage Dictionary, 2d college ed)

nodes.label: Christian Science
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Christian Science as: A religion founded by Mary Baker Eddy in 1866 that was organized under the official name of the Church of Christ, Scientist. It includes the practice of spiritual healing.

nodes.label: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints as: A group of religious bodies tracing their origin to Joseph Smith in 1830 and accepting the Book of Mormon as divine revelation. (from Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed)

nodes.label: Eastern Orthodoxy
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Eastern Orthodoxy as: The name given to the religion of the body of modern churches, including among others the Greek and Russian Orthodox, that is derived from the church of the Byzantine Empire, adheres to the Byzantine rite, and acknowledges the honorary primacy of the patriarch of Constantinople. (from American Heritage Dictionary of the English Language, 4th ed)

nodes.label: Protestantism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Protestantism as: The name given to all Christian denominations, sects, or groups rising out of the Reformation. Protestant churches generally agree that the principle of authority should be the Scriptures rather than the institutional church or the pope. (from W.L. Reese, Dictionary of Philosophy and Religion, 1999)

nodes.label: Saints
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Saints as: Persons officially recognized or acknowledged as pre-eminent for consecration, holiness, and piety, especially through canonization by a branch of the Christian church. (From Webster, 3d ed)

nodes.label: Spirit Possession
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Spirit Possession as: The idea that abnormal behavior or a medical condition is evidence that a person is under the control of a supernatural power or spirit. This belief was most commonly held in religion and medicine of the medieval period and is also held in many tribal cultures today.

nodes.label: Spirituality
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Spirituality as: Sensitivity or attachment to religious values, or to things of the spirit as opposed to material or worldly interests. (from Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed, and Oxford English Dictionary, 2nd ed)

nodes.label: Confucianism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Confucianism as: A school of thought and set of moral, ethical, and political teachings usually considered to be founded by Confucius in 6th-5th century B.C. China. (from Cambridge Dictionary of Philosophy, 1995)

nodes.label: Mysticism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Mysticism as: A philosophy based upon spiritual intuition that is believed to transcend ordinary sensory experiences or understanding.

nodes.label: Spiritualism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Spiritualism as: Religious philosophy expressing the fundamental belief that departed spirits may be contacted by the living through a medium.

nodes.label: Yoga
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Yoga as: A major orthodox system of Hindu philosophy based on Sankhya (metaphysical dualism) but differing from it in being theistic and characterized by the teaching of raja-yoga as a practical method of liberating the self. It includes a system of exercises for attaining bodily or mental control and well-being with liberation of the self and union with the universal spirit. (From Webster, 3d ed)

nodes.label: Social Sciences
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Social Sciences as: Disciplines concerned with the interrelationships of individuals in a social environment including social organizations and institutions. Includes Sociology and Anthropology.

nodes.label: Environment Design
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Environment Design as: The structuring of the environment to permit or promote specific patterns of behavior.

nodes.label: Forecasting
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forecasting as: The prediction or projection of the nature of future problems or existing conditions based upon the extrapolation or interpretation of existing scientific data or by the application of scientific methodology.

nodes.label: Government
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Government as: The complex of political institutions, laws, and customs through which the function of governing is carried out in a specific political unit.

nodes.label: Government Programs
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Government Programs as: Programs and activities sponsored or administered by local, state, or national governments.

nodes.label: Internationality
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Internationality as: The quality or state of relating to or affecting two or more nations. (After Merriam-Webster Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed)

nodes.label: Policy
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Policy as: A course or method of action selected to guide and determine present and future decisions.

nodes.label: Political Systems
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Political Systems as: The units based on political theory and chosen by countries under which their governmental power is organized and administered to their citizens.

nodes.label: Politics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Politics as: Activities concerned with governmental policies, functions, etc.

nodes.label: Private Sector
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Private Sector as: That distinct portion of the institutional, industrial, or economic structure of a country that is controlled or owned by non-governmental, private interests.

nodes.label: Public Sector
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Public Sector as: The area of a nation's economy that is tax-supported and under government control.

nodes.label: Quality of Life
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Quality of Life as: A generic concept reflecting concern with the modification and enhancement of life attributes, e.g., physical, political, moral, social environment as well as health and disease.

nodes.label: Work-Life Balance
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Work-Life Balance as: Complex ongoing balance between a person's working life and private life.

nodes.label: Anthropology, Medical
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Anthropology, Medical as: Field of social science that is concerned with differences between human groups as related to health status and beliefs.

nodes.label: Intersectional Framework
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Intersectional Framework as: Interconnections of social categorizations such as race, class, and gender, creating overlapping and interdependent systems of discrimination or disadvantage.

nodes.label: Media Exposure
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Media Exposure as: The extent to which individuals encounter messages and content via COMMUNICATION MEDIA.

nodes.label: Sociology, Medical
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Sociology, Medical as: The study of the social determinants and social effects of health and disease, and of the social structure of medical institutions or professions.

nodes.label: Crime
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Crime as: A violation of the criminal law, i.e., a breach of the conduct code specifically sanctioned by the state, which through its administrative agencies prosecutes offenders and imposes and administers punishments. The concept includes unacceptable actions whether prosecuted or going unpunished.

nodes.label: Criminal Law
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Criminal Law as: A branch of law that defines criminal offenses, regulates the apprehension, charging and trial of suspected persons, and fixes the penalties and modes of treatment applicable to convicted offenders.

nodes.label: Forensic Sciences
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Sciences as: Disciplines that apply sciences to law. Forensic sciences include a wide range of disciplines, such as FORENSIC TOXICOLOGY ; FORENSIC ANTHROPOLOGY ; FORENSIC MEDICINE ; FORENSIC DENTISTRY ; and others.

nodes.label: Age Distribution
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Age Distribution as: The frequency of different ages or age groups in a given population. The distribution may refer to either how many or what proportion of the group. The population is usually patients with a specific disease but the concept is not restricted to humans and is not restricted to medicine.

nodes.label: Censuses
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Censuses as: Enumerations of populations usually recording identities of all persons in every place of residence with age or date of birth, sex, occupation, national origin, language, marital status, income, relation to head of household, information on the dwelling place, education, literacy, health-related data (e.g., permanent disability), etc. The census or numbering of the people is mentioned several times in the Old Testament. Among the Romans, censuses were intimately connected with the enumeration of troops before and after battle and probably a military necessity. (From Last, A Dictionary of Epidemiology, 3d ed; Garrison, An Introduction to the History of Medicine, 4th ed, p66, p119)

nodes.label: Family Characteristics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Family Characteristics as: Size and composition of the family.

nodes.label: Health Status
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Health Status as: The level of health of the individual, group, or population as subjectively assessed by the individual or by more objective measures.

nodes.label: Population Dynamics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Population Dynamics as: The pattern of any process, or the interrelationship of phenomena, which affects growth or change within a population.

nodes.label: Sex Distribution
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Sex Distribution as: The number of males and females in a given population. The distribution may refer to how many men or women or what proportion of either in the group. The population is usually patients with a specific disease but the concept is not restricted to humans and is not restricted to medicine.

nodes.label: Capitalism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Capitalism as: A political and economic system characterized by individual rights, by private or corporate ownership of capital goods, and by prices, production, and the distribution of goods that are determined mainly by competition in a free market. (From Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed)

nodes.label: Economic Development
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Economic Development as: Mobilization of human, financial, capital, physical and or natural resources to generate goods and services.

nodes.label: Economic Recession
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Economic Recession as: Significant decline in economic activity spread across the economy, lasting more than a few months, normally visible in real gross domestic product, real income, employment, industrial production, and wholesale-retail sales. (National Bureau of Economic Research, Inc, www.nber.org/cycles.html, accessed 4/23/2009)

nodes.label: Expropriation
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Expropriation as: Taking of goods, property, or right of use by GOVERNMENT or others.

nodes.label: Gross Domestic Product
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Gross Domestic Product as: Value of all final goods and services produced in a country in one year.

nodes.label: Resource Allocation
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Resource Allocation as: Societal or individual decisions about the equitable distribution of available resources.

nodes.label: Universal Design
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Universal Design as: The design of products and environments to be usable by all people, to the greatest extent possible, without the need for adaption or specialized design.

nodes.label: Climate Models
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Climate Models as: Computer representations that simulate or predict the behavior or activity of WEATHER systems, processes, or phenomena.

nodes.label: Population Forecast
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Population Forecast as: Estimates of projected population.

nodes.label: Federal Government
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Federal Government as: The level of governmental organization and function at the national or country-wide level.

nodes.label: Government Agencies
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Government Agencies as: Administrative units of government responsible for policy making and management of governmental activities.

nodes.label: Local Government
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Local Government as: Smallest political subdivisions within a country at which general governmental functions are carried-out.

nodes.label: State Government
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes State Government as: The level of governmental organization and function below that of the national or country-wide government.

nodes.label: Civil Defense
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Civil Defense as: Preventive emergency measures and programs designed to protect the individual or community in times of hostile attack or natural disaster.

nodes.label: Postal Service
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Postal Service as: The functions and activities carried out by the U.S. Postal Service, foreign postal services, and private postal services such as Federal Express.

nodes.label: International Cooperation
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes International Cooperation as: The interaction of persons or groups of persons representing various nations in the pursuit of a common goal or interest.

nodes.label: Fiscal Policy
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Fiscal Policy as: Use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy.

nodes.label: Social Control Policies
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Social Control Policies as: Decisions for determining and guiding present and future objectives from among alternatives.

nodes.label: Apartheid
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Apartheid as: A former political system in SOUTH AFRICA which enforced segregation in all forms, including physical, political, legal and economic discrimination, against all non-white, non-European racial groups.

nodes.label: Colonialism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Colonialism as: The aggregate of various economic, political, and social policies by which an imperial power maintains or extends its control over other areas or peoples. It includes the practice of or belief in acquiring and retaining colonies. The emphasis is less on its identity as an ideological political system than on its designation in a period of history. (Webster, 3d ed; from Dr. J. Cassedy, NLM History of Medicine Division)

nodes.label: Communism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Communism as: A totalitarian system of government in which a single authoritarian party controls state-owned means of production with the professed aim of establishing a classless society.

nodes.label: Democracy
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Democracy as: A system of government in which there is free and equal participation by the people in the political decision-making process.

nodes.label: Fascism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Fascism as: Political movement which combines nationalism with demands for political and social renewal. Characteristics include militaristic nationalism, belief in a natural social hierarchy and the rule of elites, and the desire to create a “people’s community”, in which individual interests would be subordinated to the good of the nation. (From www.britannica.com/topic/fascism)

nodes.label: National Socialism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes National Socialism as: The doctrines and policies of the Nazis or the National Social German Workers party, which ruled Germany under Adolf Hitler from 1933-1945. These doctrines and policies included racist nationalism, expansionism, and state control of the economy. (from Columbia Encyclopedia, 6th ed. and American Heritage College Dictionary, 3d ed.)

nodes.label: Socialism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Socialism as: A system of government in which means of production and distribution of goods are controlled by the state.

nodes.label: Diplomacy
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Diplomacy as: The art and practice of conducting negotiations between people, nations or other parties such as organizations.

nodes.label: Environmentalism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Environmentalism as: Advocacy for the preservation, restoration, or improvement of the natural environment. It aims to reduce the impact of human activities on the earth and its inhabitants.

nodes.label: Lobbying
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Lobbying as: A process whereby representatives of a particular interest group attempt to influence governmental decision makers to accept the policy desires of the lobbying organization.

nodes.label: Political Activism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Political Activism as: Active involvement in the political process including promoting, impeding or raising awareness of a certain issue or set of issues.

nodes.label: Politicization
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Politicization as: Generally an issue or an institution emerging into the sphere of politics such as making previously unpolitical matters political. (Tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/13501763.2019.1619188)

nodes.label: Stakeholder Participation
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Stakeholder Participation as: A process between an entity and those groups or individuals potentially or actually impacted by the actions of that entity over a range of activities and approaches.

nodes.label: Voting
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Voting as: Method by which an individual or a group, such as in a meeting or an electorate, can engage for the purpose of making a collective decision or expressing an opinion.

nodes.label: Informal Sector
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Informal Sector as: A component of the private sector characterized by ease of entry; reliance on indigenous resources; family ownership; small scale operations; skills acquired outside of the formal sector; and unregulated markets.

nodes.label: Psychological Well-Being
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Psychological Well-Being as: Condition of existence, or state of awareness, in which psychological needs are satisfied

nodes.label: Abortion, Illegal
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Abortion, Illegal as: Illegal termination of pregnancy.

nodes.label: Body Packing
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Body Packing as: Concealing of drugs within the gastrointestinal tract or other body orifice for purposes of DRUG SMUGGLING or to avoid detection by law enforcement. Contraband other than drugs is also sometimes smuggled this way.

nodes.label: Corpse Dismemberment
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Corpse Dismemberment as: Disjoining the limbs or other parts of a corpse, often in association with criminal acts.

nodes.label: Defamation
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Defamation as: Public false statements that are illegal and damaging to the reputation of a person, group, business, organization, or institution.

nodes.label: Drug Trafficking
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Drug Trafficking as: The illegal acquisition, sale, production, transport, movement, and distribution of controlled substances such as narcotics.

nodes.label: Euthanasia, Involuntary
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Euthanasia, Involuntary as: The act or practice of killing or withholding life-sustaining treatment from a person with a medical condition, especially PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES , without INFORMED CONSENT , despite the MENTAL COMPETENCY of the person to give consent.

nodes.label: Fraud
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Fraud as: Exploitation through misrepresentation of the facts or concealment of the purposes of the exploiter.

nodes.label: Grave Robbing
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Grave Robbing as: Stealing of corpses after burial, especially for medical dissection. In the late 18th and early 19th centuries, in the absence of laws governing the acquisition of dissecting material for the study of anatomy, the needs of anatomy classes were met by surreptitious methods: body-snatching and grave robbing. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed; from Garrison, An Introduction to the History of Medicine, 4th ed, p447; from Castiglioni, A History of Medicine, 2d ed, p676)

nodes.label: Homicide
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Homicide as: The killing of one person by another.

nodes.label: Medical Neglect
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Medical Neglect as: Failure to seek timely and appropriate care or allow such care for medical, dental or psychological needs by family members, legal guardian and other caregivers. Negligence by professionals is PROFESSIONAL NEGLIGENCE .

nodes.label: Prescription Drug Diversion
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Prescription Drug Diversion as: The transfer of prescription drugs from legal to illegal distribution and marketing networks.

nodes.label: Recidivism
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Recidivism as: Repeated criminal behavior.

nodes.label: Sex Offenses
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Sex Offenses as: Any violation of established legal or moral codes in respect to sexual behavior.

nodes.label: Theft
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Theft as: Unlawful act of taking property.

nodes.label: Violence
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Violence as: Use of physical force causing or intent to cause harm, injury or abuse.

nodes.label: War Crimes
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes War Crimes as: Criminal acts committed during, or in connection with, war, e.g., maltreatment of prisoners, willful killing of civilians, etc.

nodes.label: Forensic Anthropology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Anthropology as: Scientific study of human skeletal remains with the express purpose of identification. This includes establishing individual identity, trauma analysis, facial reconstruction, photographic superimposition, determination of time interval since death, and crime-scene recovery. Forensic anthropologists do not certify cause of death but provide data to assist in determination of probable cause. This is a branch of the field of physical anthropology and qualified individuals are certified by the American Board of Forensic Anthropology. (From Am J Forensic Med Pathol 1992 Jun;13(2):146)

nodes.label: Forensic Ballistics
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Ballistics as: The science of studying projectiles in motion, ballistics, being applied to law. Ballistics on firearm projectiles, such as bullets, include the study of what happens inside the weapon, during the flight of the projectile, and when the projectile strikes the target, such as body tissue.

nodes.label: Forensic Dentistry
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Dentistry as: The application of dental knowledge to questions of law.

nodes.label: Forensic Entomology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Entomology as: The use of insects and related arthropods that inhabit decomposing corpses or remains in the conduct of medico-legal or medico-criminal investigations.

nodes.label: Forensic Imaging
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Imaging as: The use of various imaging and image enhancement techniques in forensic investigative disciplines. It often includes FORENSIC MEDICINE platforms such as X-RAYS ; CT XRAY; and MRI.

nodes.label: Forensic Microbiology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Microbiology as: The scientific discipline dedicated to analyzing evidence from BIOTERRORISM , biocrime, HOAX , or inadvertent microorganism/toxin release for attribution purposes.

nodes.label: Forensic Nursing
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Nursing as: The application of NURSING knowledge to questions of law. It is a specialty of nursing practice involving victims of crime which includes not only attending to the physical and emotional distress of victims, but also the identifying, collecting, and preserving evidence for law enforcement and the criminal justice system.

nodes.label: Forensic Psychology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Psychology as: A specialty in professional psychology characterized by activities primarily intended to provide professional psychological expertise within the judicial and legal systems.

nodes.label: Forensic Toxicology
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Forensic Toxicology as: The application of TOXICOLOGY knowledge to questions of law.

nodes.label: Birth Intervals
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Birth Intervals as: The lengths of intervals between births to women in the population.

nodes.label: Birth Order
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Birth Order as: The sequence in which children are born into the family.

nodes.label: Family Structure
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Family Structure as: Structural nature of relationships among members of a household typically in reference to a MINOR residing in the same home. More broadly any organizational framework that determines family membership, and the functions and hierarchical position of family members (https://eric.ed.gov/?qt=Family+Structure&ti=Family+Structure).

nodes.label: Marital Status
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Marital Status as: A demographic parameter indicating a person's status with respect to marriage, divorce, widowhood, singleness ( SINGLE PERSON ), etc.

nodes.label: Geriatric Assessment
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Geriatric Assessment as: Evaluation of the level of physical, physiological, or mental functioning in the older population group.

nodes.label: Health Inequities
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Health Inequities as: Differences in health status and in the distribution of health resources between different population groups, arising from the social conditions in which people are born, grow, live, work and age (https://www.who.int/news-room/facts-in-pictures/detail/health-inequities-and-their-causes#:~:text=Health%20inequities%20are%20differences%20in,right%20mix%20of%20government%20policies.)

nodes.label: Nutritional Status
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Nutritional Status as: State of the body in relation to the consumption and utilization of nutrients.

nodes.label: Social Determinants of Health
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Social Determinants of Health as: The circumstances in which people are born, grow up, live, work, and age, as well as the systems put in place to deal with illness. These circumstances are in turn shaped by a wider set of forces: economics, social policies, and politics (http://www.cdc.gov/socialdeterminants/).

nodes.label: Health Transition
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Health Transition as: Demographic and epidemiologic changes that have occurred in the last five decades in many developing countries and that are characterized by major growth in the number and proportion of middle-aged and elderly persons and in the frequency of the diseases that occur in these age groups. The health transition is the result of efforts to improve maternal and child health via primary care and outreach services and such efforts have been responsible for a decrease in the birth rate; reduced maternal mortality; improved preventive services; reduced infant mortality, and the increased life expectancy that defines the transition. (From Ann Intern Med 1992 Mar 15;116(6):499-504)

nodes.label: Human Migration
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Human Migration as: Dispersion or dislocation of people from their country of origin, either voluntarily or involuntarily.

nodes.label: Population Control
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Population Control as: Includes mechanisms or programs which control the numbers of individuals in a population of humans or animals.

nodes.label: Population Growth
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Population Growth as: Increase, over a specific period of time, in the number of individuals living in a country or region.

nodes.label: Sex Ratio
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Sex Ratio as: The number of males per 100 females.

nodes.label: Industrial Development
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Industrial Development as: Activity concerned with the planning and building of industries through manufacturing, provision of specialized services, and COMMERCE .

nodes.label: Developing Countries
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Developing Countries as: Countries in the process of change with economic growth, that is, an increase in production, per capita consumption, and income. The process of economic growth involves better utilization of natural and human resources, which results in a change in the social, political, and economic structures.

nodes.label: Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Infections as: Invasion of the host organism by microorganisms or their toxins or by parasites that can cause pathological conditions or diseases.

nodes.label: Neoplasms
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Neoplasms as: New abnormal growth of tissue. Malignant neoplasms show a greater degree of anaplasia and have the properties of invasion and metastasis, compared to benign neoplasms.

nodes.label: Cardiovascular Diseases
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Cardiovascular Diseases as: Pathological conditions involving the CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM including the HEART ; the BLOOD VESSELS ; or the PERICARDIUM .

nodes.label: Nervous System Diseases
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Nervous System Diseases as: Diseases of the central and peripheral nervous system. This includes disorders of the brain, spinal cord, cranial nerves, peripheral nerves, nerve roots, autonomic nervous system, neuromuscular junction, and muscle.

nodes.label: Respiratory Tract Diseases
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Respiratory Tract Diseases as: Diseases involving the RESPIRATORY SYSTEM .

nodes.label: Digestive System Diseases
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Digestive System Diseases as: Diseases in any part of the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT or the accessory organs ( LIVER ; BILIARY TRACT ; PANCREAS ).

nodes.label: Musculoskeletal Diseases
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Musculoskeletal Diseases as: Diseases of the muscles and their associated ligaments and other connective tissue and of the bones and cartilage viewed collectively.

nodes.label: Endocrine System Diseases
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Endocrine System Diseases as: Pathological processes of the ENDOCRINE GLANDS , and diseases resulting from abnormal level of available HORMONES .

nodes.label: Immune System Diseases
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Immune System Diseases as: Disorders caused by abnormal or absent immunologic mechanisms, whether humoral, cell-mediated, or both.

nodes.label: Mental Disorders
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Mental Disorders as: Psychiatric illness or diseases manifested by breakdowns in the adaptational process expressed primarily as abnormalities of thought, feeling, and behavior producing either distress or impairment of function.

nodes.label: Wounds and Injuries
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Wounds and Injuries as: Damage inflicted on the body as the direct or indirect result of an external force, with or without disruption of structural continuity.

nodes.label: Hemic and Lymphatic Diseases
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Hemic and Lymphatic Diseases as: Hematologic diseases and diseases of the lymphatic system collectively. Hemic diseases include disorders involving the formed elements (e.g., ERYTHROCYTE AGGREGATION, INTRAVASCULAR ) and chemical components (e.g., BLOOD PROTEIN DISORDERS ); lymphatic diseases include disorders relating to lymph, lymph nodes, and lymphocytes.

nodes.label: Aneurysm, Infected
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Aneurysm, Infected as: Aneurysm due to growth of microorganisms in the arterial wall, or infection arising within preexisting arteriosclerotic aneurysms.

nodes.label: Arthritis, Infectious
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Arthritis, Infectious as: Arthritis caused by BACTERIA ; RICKETTSIA ; MYCOPLASMA ; VIRUSES ; FUNGI ; or PARASITES .

nodes.label: Asymptomatic Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Asymptomatic Infections as: Infections that do not exhibit symptoms.

nodes.label: Bacterial Infections and Mycoses
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Bacterial Infections and Mycoses as: Infections caused by bacteria and fungi, general, specified, or unspecified.

nodes.label: Bone Diseases, Infectious
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Bone Diseases, Infectious as: Bone diseases caused by pathogenic microorganisms.

nodes.label: Breakthrough Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Breakthrough Infections as: Infections by the same infectious agent (e.g., virus, fungus) occurring during exposure to prophylaxis, vaccine and treatment.

nodes.label: Cardiovascular Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Cardiovascular Infections as: Pathological conditions of the CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM caused by infections.

nodes.label: Catheter-Related Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Catheter-Related Infections as: Infections resulting from the use of catheters. Proper aseptic technique, site of catheter placement, material composition, and virulence of the organism are all factors that can influence possible infection.

nodes.label: Central Nervous System Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Central Nervous System Infections as: Pathogenic infections of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges. DNA VIRUS INFECTIONS ; RNA VIRUS INFECTIONS ; BACTERIAL INFECTIONS ; MYCOPLASMA INFECTIONS ; SPIROCHAETALES INFECTIONS ; fungal infections; PROTOZOAN INFECTIONS ; HELMINTHIASIS ; and PRION DISEASES may involve the central nervous system as a primary or secondary process.

nodes.label: Coinfection
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Coinfection as: Simultaneous infection of a host organism by two or more pathogens. In virology, coinfection commonly refers to simultaneous infection of a single cell by two or more different viruses.

nodes.label: Communicable Diseases
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Communicable Diseases as: An illness caused by an infectious agent or its toxins that occurs through the direct or indirect transmission of the infectious agent or its products from an infected individual or via an animal, vector or the inanimate environment to a susceptible animal or human host.

nodes.label: Community-Acquired Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Community-Acquired Infections as: Any infection acquired in the community, that is, contrasted with those acquired in a health care facility ( CROSS INFECTION ). An infection would be classified as community-acquired if the patient had not recently been in a health care facility or been in contact with someone who had been recently in a health care facility.

nodes.label: Cross Infection
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Cross Infection as: Any infection which a patient contracts in a health-care institution.

nodes.label: Eye Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Eye Infections as: Infection, moderate to severe, caused by bacteria, fungi, or viruses, which occurs either on the external surface of the eye or intraocularly with probable inflammation, visual impairment, or blindness.

nodes.label: Focal Infection
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Focal Infection as: An infection at a specific location that may spread to another region of the body.

nodes.label: Gingivitis
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Gingivitis as: Inflammation of gum tissue ( GINGIVA ) without loss of connective tissue.

nodes.label: Hepatitis, Animal
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Hepatitis, Animal as: INFLAMMATION of the LIVER in non-human animals.

nodes.label: Intraabdominal Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Intraabdominal Infections as: Infection within the PERITONEAL CAVITY. A frequent cause is an ANASTOMOTIC LEAK following surgery.

nodes.label: Laboratory Infection
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Laboratory Infection as: Accidentally acquired infection in laboratory workers.

nodes.label: Latent Infection
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Latent Infection as: Delayed infection of the host by a dormant or inactive pathogen.

nodes.label: Opportunistic Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Opportunistic Infections as: An infection caused by an organism which becomes pathogenic under certain conditions, e.g., during immunosuppression.

nodes.label: Parasitic Diseases
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Parasitic Diseases as: Infections or infestations with PARASITES . They are often contracted through contact with an intermediate vector, but may occur as the result of direct exposure.

nodes.label: Pelvic Infection
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Pelvic Infection as: Infection involving the tissues or organs in the PELVIS .

nodes.label: Persistent Infection
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Persistent Infection as: Infection which lasts for a long period with continuous display of clinical features. Persistent infection arises due to inability of host cells to clear primary infections completely. When persistent infections are cleared so that infection symptoms are under control they are often referred to as chronic infections. LATENT INFECTIONS are infections in which manifestation of clinical symptoms appear later.

nodes.label: Poult Enteritis Mortality Syndrome
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Poult Enteritis Mortality Syndrome as: An acute, transmissible, infectious disease associated with high MORTALITY and MORBIDITY in young turkeys (poults). It is characterized by DIARRHEA ; ANOREXIA ; growth depression, and immune dysfunction. The cause is unknown but astroviruses ( AVASTROVIRUS ) and coronaviruses ( CORONAVIRUS, TURKEY ) have been isolated from diseased poults and are thought to cause the enteritis and increased susceptibility to bacterial infections.

nodes.label: Pregnancy Complications, Infectious
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Pregnancy Complications, Infectious as: The co-occurrence of pregnancy and an INFECTION . The infection may precede or follow FERTILIZATION .

nodes.label: Prosthesis-Related Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Prosthesis-Related Infections as: Infections resulting from the implantation of prosthetic devices. The infections may be acquired from intraoperative contamination (early) or hematogenously acquired from other sites (late).

nodes.label: Reproductive Tract Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Reproductive Tract Infections as: Infections of the genital tract in females or males. They can be caused by endogenous, iatrogenic, or sexually transmitted organisms.

nodes.label: Respiratory Tract Infections
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Respiratory Tract Infections as: Invasion of the host RESPIRATORY SYSTEM by microorganisms, usually leading to pathological processes or diseases.

nodes.label: Sepsis
nodes.summary: NLM MeSH describes Sepsis as: Systemic inflammatory response syndrome with a proven or suspected infectious etiology.
